In 2022, the HKMA engaged a company for the first time to conduct a waste audit to gain a clearer understanding of the composition of waste generated in its daily operations (plastics, paper, metals, glass, wood, electronics, etc.) and to receive waste reduction recommendations. Based on the audit findings, the HKMA launched a food waste recycling programme in November, placing food waste collection bins in all pantries. The food waste collected daily is transported to an organic resource recovery centre in Hong Kong, where it is converted into renewable energy for electricity generation. The residuals from the conversion process can also be made into compost for landscaping and agricultural use. Furthermore, recycling bins are conveniently placed at various locations throughout the offices. The HKMA shares recycling tips with staff and places greater emphasis on improving source separation of recyclables, as well as guidelines on handling items such as cardboard boxes, food containers, and beverage bottles. In addition, activities are regularly held to raise staff environmental awareness, explain waste management policies, and encourage staff to make good use of the recycling facilities in the office.  Food waste collected daily is transported to an organic resource recovery centre Recycling plastic items  The HKMA operates two data centres (primary and backup). As they account for a major portion of the organisation's overall energy consumption, the HKMA has adopted green design and various energy-saving measures, including in-row cooling systems, LED lighting, and round-the-clock power usage effectiveness monitoring. Following the completion of a consultancy study on the green performance of these data centres in 2022, the HKMA is preparing to implement recommendations to enhance overall energy efficiency. Preparations are also under way to obtain green data centre certification.  Recognising the importance of cultivating a sustainability culture, the HKMA regularly launches programmes and activities to educate and encourage staff to adopt sustainability-friendly habits and embrace green and digitalised working practices. The HKMA shares green living tips and annual office-wide energy consumption and paper usage statistics with staff to remind them to help address environmental matters at the individual level, and also encourages staff to put forward suggestions on sustainability matters. Under the leadership of a Senior Manager in the Administration Division, a focus group brings together staff from different departments to brainstorm ideas and concrete measures for promoting a greener working environment. Focus group members also serve as ambassadors when new green measures are introduced.  The HKMA encourages the wider community to adopt more environmentally friendly practices and has introduced various measures to enhance operational efficiency across the HKMA, the financial industry, and the broader economy, with a view to minimising resource consumption.  The HKMA's Supervisory and Regulatory Data Submission System (STET) is a one-stop platform for banks to submit documents electronically to the HKMA, covering various periodic returns submitted on a weekly, monthly, quarterly, or annual basis. Another system, e-Delivery, is a secure electronic communication channel for the HKMA to issue circulars, guidelines, and other information to banks. Both systems help save a substantial amount of paper each year.  In handling bank complaints and enforcement work, the HKMA has taken steps to support paperless document submission, allowing bank customers to lodge complaints through electronic channels and by completing online forms. The HKMA is also developing a new-generation management information system to facilitate complaints processing and the transition from paper-based to digital records.  To reduce paper usage, the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU) has adopted digital signatures in its daily communications with participants, including the issuance of circulars, account opening and account termination letters, and replies to audit confirmations. Looking ahead, the CMU will continue to explore further green measures, including the adoption of automated electronic processes for both internal and external communications.  The HKMA promotes greater use of electronic payments in place of cash and physical cheques by encouraging the use of the Faster Payment System (FPS) and stored value facilities (SVFs). Further information on FPS and SVFs is contained in the "Hong Kong as an International Financial Centre" chapter of the HKMA Annual Report 2022.  Sending electronic red packets (e-laisee) is simple, convenient, and helps reduce the use of physical red packet envelopes and banknotes, thereby contributing to sustainable development in Hong Kong. To this end, the HKMA has continued to actively promote e-laisee across various social media and traditional platforms, encouraging the public to send e-laisee via online or mobile banking services using FPS or other e-wallet services during the Lunar New Year. Banks and e-wallet operators have also organised various activities to attract users to adopt e-laisee, such as offering festive user interfaces, enhancing features for greater convenience, and launching lucky draws or cashback promotions.  The HKMA promotes e-laisee on social media platforms  For members of the public who choose to send physical red packets during the Lunar New Year, the HKMA continues to encourage the use of "fit notes" — previously circulated but still crisp banknotes — for this purpose. Fit notes reduce the need to print new banknotes, thereby minimising the environmental impact. Feedback from note-issuing banks indicates that public acceptance of fit notes has been growing in recent years.  The Coin Collection Programme reflects the HKMA's efforts to promote coin recycling. Coins collected through the programme are returned to circulation to meet public demand, improving the efficiency of coin circulation and reducing the need for minting. The programme operates two coin collection vehicles and has served over one million users to date, collecting more than 800 million coins with a total face value of approximately HK$1.3 billion. In 2022, approximately 78% of users chose to add part or all of the value of their coins to their stored value facility accounts. The HKMA has maintained its collaboration with the HKCSS by deploying coin collection vehicles on flag selling days organised by non-governmental organisations (NGOs), in support of social services.  Coin counting machines on the coin collection vehicles  Launched in 2014, the Coin Collection Programme was the world's first systematic coin collection programme to adopt a mobile vehicle concept. Over the years, it has received numerous local and international awards in recognition of its innovative and environmentally friendly approach to coin handling. The programme operates two coin collection vehicles, each equipped with two high-speed coin counting machines to collect coins exchanged by the public. Members of the public may choose to exchange their coins for banknotes, add the value to their stored value facility (such as an Octopus card or e-wallet) accounts, or donate the proceeds to the Community Chest as a charitable contribution. In addition to collecting coins, the vehicles are periodically deployed for various educational activities, such as student visits.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) conducted an independent verification of the climate targets (the "Climate Targets") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (the "HKMA"). The Climate Targets were developed with reference to the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Manual (the "SBTi Corporate Manual"). The purpose of this verification was to verify whether the Climate Targets were developed with reference to the SBTi Corporate Manual. This verification was conducted in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised) "Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board (IAASB). The verification procedures were designed to express an opinion and conclusion to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was carried out in accordance with the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Manual. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of data. Our verification work was conducted in a completely independent and impartial manner. Based on the results of this verification, HKQAA provides reasonable assurance and concludes that: • The Climate Targets were developed with reference to the SBTi Corporate Manual. Shen Xiaoyin, Verification Manager, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2023  Verification Statement  The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) conducted an independent verification of the 2022 Environmental Data (the "2022 Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (the "HKMA"). The 2022 Data covers total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emission intensity, paper consumption intensity, non-hazardous waste generation intensity and recycling rate for 2022, as well as the changes in these data compared to 2015 levels. The HKMA's greenhouse gas emissions data was compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (the "GHG Protocol") jointly published by the World Resources Institute (the "WRI") and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (the "WBCSD"). The scope of verification covered relevant data for the period from 1 January 2022 to 31 December 2022, as well as relevant data for the period from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 used for annual performance comparison. The scope of verification encompassed a total of 6 office and warehouse assets: 4 offices at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, and 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and 2 warehouses at 5) Loksang Industrial Centre and 6) Chung Lee Centre, located in Kwai Chung and Tsuen Wan respectively. The purpose of the verification was to provide reasonable assurance on the accuracy and reliability of the 2022 Data, and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanisms. Within the scope of verification, HKQAA examined representative data and supporting evidence selected from the 6 assets. This verification was conducted in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised) "Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board (IAASB). The verification procedures were designed to express an opinion and conclusion to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of data by tracing selected sample data back to their sources, and also examined the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation and internal checking, as well as conducting reliability testing. The verification process also included verifying internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with representatives responsible for preparing the 2022 Data, and selecting representative data and information for review. The relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of data. Our verification work was conducted in a completely independent and impartial manner. The HKQAA verification team did not participate in the preparation of the 2022 Data. Based on the results of this verification, HKQAA provides reasonable assurance and concludes on the 2022 Data that: • The 2022 Data is materially accurate and reliable; • The HKMA's overall data collection mechanisms are adequate. Shen Xiaoyin, Verification Manager, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2023

Scaling up and accelerating climate action has become the most pressing challenge of our time. We are now almost halfway through the critical decade for addressing the climate crisis. We need to reduce global carbon emissions by more than 40% during this decade if we are to have any hope of keeping global warming within 1.5 degrees Celsius. Yet greenhouse gas emissions continue to reach new records. The latest climate science indicates that the window for limiting global temperature rise to 1.5 degrees Celsius is closing rapidly. The impacts of a 1.1-degree rise in temperature are already being felt acutely around the world — record-breaking heatwaves and droughts, severe flooding and storms, and other extreme weather events are occurring with increasing frequency and intensity across the globe. Hong Kong is no exception. Last September, we were struck by a powerful super typhoon, followed immediately by a once-in-a-century rainstorm. Despite our well-developed infrastructure and rapid emergency response capabilities, the impact was severe — widespread flooding, major transport disruption, and damage to roads in multiple locations. All of this serves as a stark reminder that bold and decisive climate action is an urgent imperative.  Asia faces particularly significant challenges on the path to low-carbon transition, especially in balancing economic development with sustainability. We need credible transition strategies that strike the right balance between climate action, economic growth, and social inclusion. This is no easy task. Given the region's rapid economic development and fast-growing population, Asia accounts for more than half of global carbon emissions. At the same time, the Asia-Pacific region is densely populated and, due to its geographic characteristics, highly vulnerable to rising sea levels and extreme weather events. As economies in the region are at different stages of development, while the low-carbon transition will create new opportunities for some, mobilising the financing needed for transition remains a formidable challenge for others. Market estimates suggest that the Asia-Pacific region will require over USD 3 trillion per year in low-carbon transition investment over the next 30 years.  As an international financial centre, Hong Kong is both well-positioned and obliged to harness the power of finance to support the low-carbon transition across Asia. In our roles as banking regulator, market facilitator, and responsible investor, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has been making significant efforts on the sustainability agenda. Readers will find details of the various specific measures and initiatives launched by the HKMA over the past year in the respective chapters of this report. In addition, to strengthen the HKMA's internal governance structure and better coordinate sustainability work across different functional areas, we established the Green and Sustainable Finance Steering Committee last year. Details of this Steering Committee can be found in the newly added "Governance of Sustainability" chapter.  Hong Kong's banks have an important role to play in supporting Asia's transition to net zero. In addition to fulfilling our traditional role as banking regulator — ensuring that banks properly manage climate risks in our day-to-day supervisory work — we also act as a facilitator, supporting the banking sector in financing the low-carbon transition. One example is the development of a green classification framework to help banks and other financial institutions identify environmentally sustainable activities, thereby aligning their business decisions with global climate objectives. We launched a prototype green classification framework for consultation in May and are currently refining it based on feedback received during the consultation period.  Furthermore, as demand grows for higher-quality and globally comparable sustainability disclosure information, the HKMA is working with other regulators to develop a clear roadmap for Hong Kong to adopt the disclosure standards issued by the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) in June — a comprehensive and globally applicable set of common sustainability reporting standards.  The HKMA's role as a facilitator goes beyond setting frameworks and rules. We are also committed to addressing pain points faced by the industry. Many banks currently face data limitations that hinder their ability to conduct physical risk assessments. In response, the HKMA will shortly launch a cloud-based physical risk assessment platform. Banks will be able to assess the impact of physical hazards on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios simply by entering a property address, thereby helping banks better manage related climate risks.  As a major international financial centre and sustainable finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong has been playing a bridging role, channelling international investment into sustainable development projects across Asia and supporting the region's low-carbon transition. In recent years, international green and sustainable bonds arranged in Hong Kong have accounted for more than one-third of the Asian market, placing Hong Kong well ahead of other jurisdictions. Of particular note, the Shenzhen Municipal Government and the Hainan Provincial Government each issued green and sustainable bonds in Hong Kong in 2023 — for the third and second consecutive years, respectively — reaffirming Hong Kong's important role as a green gateway connecting Mainland China with the rest of the world.  Hong Kong's vibrant sustainable bond activity is in part attributable to the catalytic effect of the Government Green Bond Programme. Since 2019, the HKMA has helped the Government issue approximately USD 25 billion in green bonds to institutional and retail investors. We have taken every issuance opportunity to innovate and expand the features of green bonds — including currency denomination, tenor, and distribution channels — laying the groundwork for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. Following the issuance of the world's largest government retail green bond in 2022, we issued the world's first tokenised government green bonds in February 2023. In February 2024, we completed the second issuance of tokenised green bonds — denominated in four major currencies and issued in digitally native form, making them the world's first multi-currency digital green bonds.  We have also proactively introduced a range of measures to enhance the vibrancy and competitiveness of Hong Kong's sustainable finance ecosystem. These span multiple areas including skills training, data improvement, green fintech, and transition finance. In particular, regarding talent development, we launched a new "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for the banking sector in 2023, providing banking practitioners with a structured curriculum to enhance their understanding and expertise in green and sustainable finance.  Transition finance is another key focus area for us. It provides funding for decarbonisation activities in high-carbon and hard-to-abate sectors, preventing those sectors from being left behind due to a lack of financial support. To support the sound development of transition finance, the HKMA will expand Hong Kong's green classification framework to cover transition activities. We will also broaden the scope of the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme — which provides subsidies to eligible bond issuers and borrowers — to include transition bonds and loans, so as to encourage regional enterprises to raise transition capital in Hong Kong. In addition, we will strengthen engagement with relevant stakeholders and leverage public-private partnerships and blended finance models to attract private sector investment into sustainable development projects that have historically been more difficult to finance.  Some of this work requires cross-sectoral collaboration and is primarily coordinated through the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group, co-chaired by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission. Regional collaboration is equally important. In addition to our long-standing partnership with the International Finance Corporation on the Green Commercial Banking Alliance, the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office joined the Sustainable Investment Capacity Building Coalition and the Green Development Investment Partnership as founding members in 2023. The Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero also announced plans to establish a chapter in Hong Kong. Through these partnerships, we aim to promote skills training and knowledge sharing, and in turn support the channelling of capital into sustainable development projects across the region and beyond.  To drive new business development and knowledge exchange, the HKMA helped organise the inaugural "Hong Kong Green Week" earlier this year, attracting over 1,600 attendees from nearly 30 jurisdictions — including top decision-makers from the global business and financial community — to discuss ways to scale up climate finance in the region and forge new partnerships.  CEO Eddie Yue delivering remarks at the Asia-Pacific Climate Business Forum, the flagship event of Hong Kong Green Week.  As the manager of Hong Kong's official reserves and a significant asset owner globally, the HKMA leads by example as a responsible investor. Since 2015, the HKMA has been pioneering investment in green and sustainable assets, progressively expanding the Exchange Fund's ESG and green asset portfolios across public and private markets. In pursuit of the goal of achieving net zero emissions in the Exchange Fund's Investment Portfolio by 2050 or earlier, the HKMA last year added an active global equity portfolio with a sustainability and climate transition theme, while extending the use of a customised low-carbon equity index to another public market asset portfolio. In addition, the HKMA prioritises investment in green, social, and sustainability bonds, which have outperformed their investment benchmarks — embodying the proposition of "doing good while doing well." In private markets, we continue to pursue green-related investment opportunities and have become an anchor investor in two Asia-focused transition investment funds. By end-2022, the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund's equity portfolio had decreased by 6% compared to 2021 and by 46% compared to 2017, consistently remaining below the overall market level.  As a sustainable institution, the HKMA will continue to strive for progress and set sustainability goals and plans built on three pillars: environment, staff, and social responsibility. Specifically, on our low-carbon transition journey, we are continuously strengthening our capacity to address climate change by assessing our environmental performance and implementing a range of internal measures. These measures encompass emissions reduction, energy efficiency improvements, and waste management, with the ultimate goal of fulfilling our commitment to achieve net zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. We have formulated plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions in the near term and are making good progress towards our 2030 interim target for Scope 2 emissions reduction.  To attract and retain the talent needed to fulfil the HKMA's important functions, beyond our green objectives, we are also committed to promoting staff health and wellbeing. Furthermore, we contribute to building a caring society by working with various stakeholders to promote financial inclusion, enhance public financial literacy, and raise public awareness of fraud prevention.  The climate challenge is immense and extraordinarily urgent. As economies around the world move towards a more sustainable future, significant changes to financing activities and asset allocation are expected along the way. This transition carries considerable risks, but it will also bring with it unprecedented opportunities. As a leading global sustainable finance hub, Hong Kong has a responsibility to take the lead in rising to these challenges. At the same time, we are well-positioned to seize the opportunities they present. The HKMA will fully support the industry in financing the low-carbon transition, continue to lead by example as a responsible investor and sustainable institution, and work with like-minded partners to advance this most important global agenda of our time.  Eddie Yue Chief Executive

Climate change risks and other sustainability issues are global in nature. The HKMA's objective in its sustainability work is to take a leadership role through its policies and operations, ensuring that Hong Kong's financial system and the HKMA itself are resilient to climate change risks and supporting the transition to more sustainable economic development. Through active participation in international and regional organisations, the HKMA will also strive to contribute to the development of regional and global green and sustainable finance policies and standards. As a banking regulator, the HKMA will further strengthen the banking sector's climate resilience and climate risk management capabilities. Specifically, key priorities include: conducting a new round of thematic reviews on banks' climate risk management practices and holding a new round of consultation meetings as part of assessing banks' progress in implementing supervisory requirements on climate risk management; continuing work on integrating climate factors into the HKMA's supervisory review process; completing the second industry-wide climate risk stress test and providing guidance to participating banks throughout the process, as well as sharing observations and lessons learned with the industry; enhancing sustainable development disclosures, including collaborating with local authorities to align relevant requirements with the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards as a global benchmark, and preparing for implementation of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's Pillar 3 framework for climate-related financial risks; and sharing with the industry guidance on best practices in transition planning. To promote the healthy development of banks in providing green and sustainable investment products, the HKMA will continue to monitor local and international market and regulatory developments and maintain engagement with the industry to ensure that banks adopt appropriate sales processes. In addition, the HKMA will also play a facilitator role, working to promote the development of the green finance ecosystem and supporting banks in financing the economic transition. We will soon publish the local green taxonomy and continue to expand its coverage to include transition activities and more. At the same time, we will continue to explore technology solutions to help banks identify, measure and monitor their climate risk exposures; one example is the cloud-based platform to be launched soon to facilitate banks' physical risk assessments. To enhance the professional competence of practitioners, we will also develop the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module at the specialist level under the "Banking Professional Qualification Framework" in 2024. Hong Kong is well-positioned to serve as a regional and international sustainable finance hub. To fulfil this role, the HKMA is assisting the Government in implementing the proposals in the 2023-24 Budget to expand the scope of the Government Green Bond Programme to cover sustainable finance projects, thereby deepening the development of the local green and sustainable bond market; and attracting more green finance activities, including transition finance activities, to Hong Kong through the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme. We will also continue to encourage more governments, institutions and corporations to raise green funds through Hong Kong, and explore the potential synergies between green finance and technology. Furthermore, we will continue to assist in implementing the Government-funded Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Programme to expand Hong Kong's green finance talent pool. As co-chair of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), we will continue to work closely with other agency departments to coordinate cross-sectoral policies and work to promote the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. The Steering Group will focus on three areas of work in 2024, namely sustainable disclosure, application of technology, and transition finance. As another key focus, through the Green Basecamp, the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation will continue to jointly roll out various dedicated programmes in Asia, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market analysis, delivering targeted professional training for banks, and offering practical guidance to help financial institutions build their customised green transition pathways. In 2024, we will also strive to deepen collaboration with the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero, the Sustainable Investment Capacity Building Coalition, and the Finance for Green Development Partnership. As a responsible investor, the HKMA is committed to achieving a net-zero emissions target for the Exchange Fund's Investment Portfolio by 2050 or earlier. We will continue to enhance the sustainability of Exchange Fund investments through a three-pronged approach to responsible investment, ensuring the portfolio's resilience throughout the journey towards net zero. Recognising that achieving an economy-wide transition is essential to meeting the goals of the Paris Agreement, we are refining our net-zero strategy to focus on assets that can generate positive climate outcomes for the real economy, while taking into account the Exchange Fund's investment objectives. As an environmentally responsible organisation, the HKMA's decarbonisation strategy will continue to evolve to reflect the latest market, regulatory, technological and other climate-related developments. To further enhance the HKMA's climate resilience and risk preparedness, we will explore the feasibility of using technology solutions to assess the impact of physical risks on our offices. In addition, we will continue to actively encourage staff to participate in our sustainability efforts, including launching campaigns to cultivate sustainable habits and optimising office processes and practices. Furthermore, the HKMA will continue to maintain a consistent, efficient and sustainable approach to procurement, including assessing suppliers' ESG practices during contract selection and renewal. Building on the green data centre certification obtained in 2023, the HKMA is committed to upholding the specified certification standards. With regard to regular upgrades of data centre facilities, in addition to keeping pace with the latest technological developments, we will also incorporate green design and operational practices. At the same time, we will continue to reduce electronic waste through the application of technology and convergence, and actively modernise internal systems to improve efficiency and minimise potential risks. Finally, in the area of social focus, the HKMA will identify more community service opportunities for colleagues, and collaborate with the industry to promote financial inclusion and enhance financial literacy, as well as raise public awareness of financial fraud prevention.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impacts. The HKMA, through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, banking regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor, and sustainable institution, contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across Asia. The HKMA has in place a robust sustainability governance framework to lead the formulation of its sustainability strategies and policies, oversee the implementation of relevant measures, and ensure that sustainability factors are embedded in the HKMA's own operations and working practices. In its commitment to good institutional governance, the HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework with clear accountability arrangements and a high degree of transparency for sustainability-related work. This governance framework ensures that sustainability factors are effectively integrated into the HKMA's strategic planning and decision-making processes, and that effective mechanisms are in place to monitor and assess the progress and effectiveness of sustainability efforts.  The HKMA's sustainability governance framework comprises: the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant sub-committees, which oversee the HKMA's work, including its sustainability work, and provide recommendations; the Green and Sustainable Finance Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which provides management-level leadership for the HKMA's overall Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) strategies and policies; with respect to responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, which coordinates and oversees ESG-related work within the Exchange Fund Investment Office; and with respect to other functional areas, relevant panels and working groups, which plan and implement sustainability measures relating to banking and market development as well as the HKMA's own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), co-initiated by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the work of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders, and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong.  In light of the significant expansion of the scope of the HKMA's sustainability work over the past few years, the Steering Committee was established in October as a new central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability work across the HKMA's different functional areas.¹ Its remit includes: providing guidance on strategies, policies, and plans for ESG-related matters across the four functional areas of banking, market development, Exchange Fund investment, and internal operations; overseeing the implementation of ESG-related initiatives by the HKMA's functional departments; assessing the HKMA's performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and overseeing external communications strategy.  The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with three Deputy Chief Executives serving as permanent members. In addition, the designated Assistant Chief Executives responsible for key functions related to green and sustainable development are invited to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on key outcomes and future plans for their respective areas of work. The Steering Committee meets on a regular basis and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA's Banking Department, Corporate Development and Administration Department, External Department, and Exchange Fund Investment Office.  In addition to developing and implementing its own sustainability measures, the HKMA co-initiated the Steering Group with the SFC in May 2020.² The Steering Group serves as a cross-agency platform to provide strategic direction and coordinate cross-sectoral work on the financial industry's response to climate and environmental risks, with a view to consolidating Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in Asia and globally. Details of the Steering Group's work are set out in the chapter "Strengthening the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem".

Climate change represents a significant risk to the financial system. The HKMA has been committed to strengthening the Hong Kong financial system to build a greener and more sustainable future, contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks are exposed to various sustainability and climate-related issues in their day-to-day business operations. To continue performing their critical functions in the financial system and channel more capital towards green and sustainable projects, banks must proactively manage climate risks. As the banking regulator, the HKMA places particular emphasis on building banks' capacity to respond to and manage climate risks, and on accelerating banks' efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. The HKMA is committed to developing different policy measures to enhance the banking system's capacity to handle climate risks. In August, the HKMA issued a circular on net-zero transition planning, setting out high-level principles to help banks maintain safety and soundness as the economy transitions to net-zero emissions. Following the issuance of that circular, we conducted a questionnaire survey with selected banks in the fourth quarter to better understand their transition planning measures. Based on the survey results, we will share observations and best practices on transition planning with the industry, and will organise seminars or workshops to facilitate experience sharing among industry participants. On the disclosure front, in light of the latest international developments — including the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards published in June, and the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's (BCBS) consultation on the Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks launched in November — the HKMA is enhancing its work to improve the sustainability-related disclosure framework for Hong Kong banks. Specifically, the HKMA is working with local authorities and stakeholders to develop a comprehensive roadmap for Hong Kong that is aligned with the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. During the year, the HKMA strengthened its supervisory oversight of banks' climate risk management and provided recommendations to banks to help them further enhance their climate resilience and climate risk management capabilities. The HKMA made significant progress in implementing its two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into the supervisory process for banks. Climate risk management has now been included as a standing agenda item in the prudential meetings held with bank management. Banking supervisors also adopted an enhanced CAMEL rating system that has incorporated climate risk factors to assess banks' risk profiles and risk management systems. As part of the implementation of the two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into the banking supervisory process, the HKMA revised the "Green" assessment framework to focus on banks' transition planning measures. The HKMA is also reviewing the Supervisory Review Process used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy levels and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with a view to encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks to address climate risks. Key work priorities in 2023 under the two-year plan: Following the conclusion of the 12-month implementation period for compliance with the Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management", the HKMA launched a round of thematic examinations on climate-related risk governance in the second quarter. The thematic examinations covered four areas, including governance structures for climate-related risks, oversight of climate strategy, oversight of climate-related risk management, and institutional culture, awareness and communication. The HKMA made a number of improvements to its climate risk stress testing framework, including the introduction of a new five-year scenario to assess the potential impact on banks of the simultaneous occurrence of economic and climate change shocks. Following these improvements, and as part of the HKMA's regular regulator-led stress testing programme, the second round of climate risk stress testing was launched in June to conduct a comprehensive assessment of banks' climate risk exposures and to further enhance banks' capacity to manage climate risks. A total of 44 banks participated in this round of stress testing, representing an increase of more than 60% compared to the first pilot exercise in 2021. The HKMA also organised a Climate Risk Stress Testing Forum in November, attended by as many as 300 banking practitioners. By facilitating the sharing of experience among banks, the event helped to deepen the industry's overall understanding of climate risk measurement. The HKMA also conducted a series of engagement meetings to review banks' progress in implementing the HKMA's Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management". The HKMA held meetings with bank management to discuss their work on climate risk management and common challenges facing the industry, and reviewed information provided by banks and other publicly available information to assess their progress. The HKMA provided targeted recommendations to banks to encourage and support them to continue strengthening their climate risk management capabilities in line with the HKMA's supervisory expectations. As global concern about climate change continues to grow and concerted efforts are made to address it, the HKMA has observed an increasing demand for green and sustainable investment products, and some banks have been offering such products to meet client needs. In view of this, the HKMA completed a thematic review of banks' sale of green and sustainable investment products, and issued a circular in November setting out the standards the HKMA expects banks to meet and sharing observations on good practices. The circular covers a number of areas including product due diligence, disclosure, governance and controls, staff training, and record-keeping, and aims to mitigate potential greenwashing risks and enhance investor confidence, thereby promoting the sound development of such investment activities. The HKMA will continue to monitor the latest trends and market developments. The HKMA is committed to promoting the use of technology in green and sustainable banking. For example, technology can improve data availability and risk analysis, enhancing banks' capacity to manage climate risks. The HKMA will soon launch a pilot version of a cloud-based platform to enable banks to assess the impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings under different climate scenarios. In addition, the HKMA continues to collaborate with other central banks and regulators to explore how technological solutions can assist with physical risk assessment. On another front, the HKMA also encourages the adoption of sustainable anti-money laundering (AML) approaches through the application of advanced analytics and artificial intelligence, reducing the consumption of compliance-related resources. In 2023, the HKMA launched an online shared data submission platform to fully automate the financial crime risk data collection process, thereby enhancing the operational workflow for banks to submit AML-related data in a sustainable manner. In September, the HKMA organised the "Green Fintech Competition", which sought market-ready solutions to help the banking industry address challenges in the following areas: (i) net-zero transition or transition planning; (ii) climate risk management; (iii) green and sustainable finance; and (iv) sustainability or climate-related disclosure and reporting. The competition attracted over 85 submissions from approximately 70 companies. In December, the HKMA organised the "Green and Sustainable Banking Symposium", providing a platform for the banking industry and the technology sector to explore the roles of low-carbon technology and green fintech in the net-zero transition in Hong Kong and the Mainland, at which the results of the "Green Fintech Competition" were also announced. The event attracted approximately 400 participants from banks, technology companies, regulatory bodies and academia. To enhance transparency across financial markets and promote greater consistency in green and sustainable finance decision-making, the HKMA, with the assistance of a consultancy firm, developed a local green taxonomy framework. In May, the HKMA published a discussion paper on the "Prototype Hong Kong Green Taxonomy", seeking stakeholder views on the establishment and implementation of a green classification catalogue. Based on the consultation results, the HKMA is fine-tuning the prototype framework and identifying additional areas for the next stage of framework development. The HKMA participates in the work of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), which has identified environmental crimes as predicate offences for money laundering, and given the nexus between AML and environmental, social and governance (ESG) considerations, this area is attracting increasing attention from more regulators. The HKMA recognises the potential risks that climate change may pose to the financial system and has therefore incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risk analysis and research to strengthen ongoing surveillance efforts. The HKMA takes climate change into consideration in its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks and incorporates analysis of climate-related risks in various financial stability reports. Through active participation in the Scenario Design and Analysis Working Group under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA helps to further enrich climate scenarios, enabling central banks and regulators to better understand the macroeconomic and financial implications of climate change. As a member of the Financial Stability Board's Workstream on Transition Planning, the HKMA participates in analysing the interaction between transition planning by financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, enabling policymakers to develop forward-looking and dynamic perspectives on climate-related financial risks. On the research front, the HKMA conducts a number of applied research projects examining the impact of climate change and broader ESG issues on the financial industry and the economy. Research topics include climate risk exposures in the banking sector and investment funds, ESG fund flows, the impact of climate change on property prices, and the spillover effects of firms' ESG performance in global supply chains. These research findings enhance the HKMA's understanding of the implications of climate change and ESG issues for financial stability and contribute to the formulation of relevant policies. At the local level, the research helps to strengthen the HKMA's ongoing surveillance and assessment of the impact of climate risks on financial stability. Externally, the HKMA also shares research findings with a broad range of stakeholders through international events on climate-related matters and various channels such as HKMA Research Memoranda. The HKMA's Liquidity Facilities Framework is a collateralised backstop funding arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has, in accordance with NGFS recommendations, incorporated sustainability considerations in the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through such engagement, the HKMA helps to facilitate international and regional policy dialogue on addressing climate change and its implications for financial stability, and draws lessons to help strengthen the climate resilience of the Hong Kong financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the HKMA is committed to raising market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and enablers, and supporting international initiatives to align with global standards. During the year, the HKMA worked closely with local and international partners to build a richer ecosystem and drive the further development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. The Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), co-led by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the financial sector's response to climate and environmental risks, accelerating the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong, and supporting the Government's climate strategies. The Steering Group has made good progress since its establishment. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced key measures to support Hong Kong in capturing sustainable finance opportunities, with major work areas covering sustainable disclosure, ecosystem capacity building, transition finance, and green fintech. Specifically, a Sustainable Disclosure Workstream has been established to develop a roadmap for Hong Kong's adoption of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. The roadmap will encompass four key areas, including sustainability reporting, assurance, data and technology, and skills training. A Transition Finance Workstream has also been established to explore approaches to support financial institutions and enterprises in transition planning and reporting. The Steering Group is also strengthening the sustainable finance ecosystem through cross-sectoral skills training and data enhancement. In particular, regarding data, we continue to promote the adoption of the Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Unlisted Companies developed by the Steering Group in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Steering Group will continue to stay abreast of the latest developments in green and sustainable finance and enhance Hong Kong's position as a regional and global green and sustainable finance hub. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced three new key workstreams to capture investment and financing opportunities arising from the low-carbon transition in the Asia-Pacific region. To support skills training for the industry, the Centre for Green and Sustainable Finance under the Steering Group implemented the Government's "Green and Sustainable Finance Talent Programme", providing subsidies to practitioners, students, and graduates who undertake green and sustainable finance-related training and obtain relevant qualifications. As of December 2023, a total of 46 international and local training courses or qualifications had been registered as eligible training or qualifications under the programme, and over 560 subsidy applications had been approved. The HKMA also introduced the Foundation Level of the new "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the "Banking Professional Qualification Framework". This module aims to promote talent development in the banking sector and enhance the overall professional competence of practitioners. In 2024, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with the banking industry to develop the Professional Level of the module to meet the rapidly growing demand for green and sustainable finance professionals in the industry. To help financial institutions and enterprises, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), better understand key climate and sustainability-related issues, including climate risk management, sustainability reporting, greenhouse gas emissions calculation, and transition planning, the HKMA co-organised a series of seminars and thematic workshops during the year with relevant Government bureaux and departments, as well as global partners such as CDP, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ) and the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF), attracting participants from the financial services and corporate sectors. For students, following the launch of the "Sustainable Finance Internship Programme" in 2022, training courses were held in January and February 2023 to deepen interns' and university graduates' understanding of sustainable finance. Recognising the potential of technology in bridging climate-related data gaps and improving data quality, the HKMA is committed to making relevant data more accessible and improving data quality to support informed decision-making and effective climate action. In February 2024, the Steering Group launched a series of website enhancements to provide financial institutions, enterprises and the public with a one-stop source of green and sustainable finance information. Key enhancements include a sustainable disclosure e-platform, greenhouse gas emissions calculation and estimation tools, as well as more centralised, accessible, and searchable data and resources. During "Hong Kong Green Week", the Steering Group also co-organised the "Tech for Sustainable Finance" event with Cyberport and InvestHK to showcase leading green innovation solutions and Hong Kong's strengths in green technology. "Hong Kong Green Week – Finance Theme" was held from 26 February to 1 March 2024, during which various sustainability-themed events attracted over 1,600 guests from nearly 30 jurisdictions, including representatives from financial institutions, corporations, central banks, international organisations, government bodies, academia, and consultancy firms. The flagship event of "Hong Kong Green Week" was the "Asia-Pacific Climate Business Forum", co-organised by the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation. The Forum brought together over 400 guests, including top decision-makers from global business and finance, to discuss solutions for unlocking climate finance in the Asia-Pacific region. The two-day event covered a wide range of topics, including energy transition, decarbonisation of heavy industries, circular economy, the future of sustainable finance, and emerging climate technologies in emerging and developing markets in the Asia-Pacific region. The Forum received support from both public and private sector organisations, with over 10 roundtables, seminars, and other exchange activities co-organised. Topics covered climate finance, carbon markets, electric vehicle supply chains, net-zero transition financing, green finance taxonomies, and green development financing in the Belt and Road region. In addition, the HKMA co-organised the "Asia Climate Finance Roundtable" with the International Monetary Fund on 29 February 2024, exploring key measures to scale up climate finance and the role of central banks and regulators in climate risk management. These events are part of the HKMA's broader efforts to promote and enrich Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance ecosystem, serving as useful platforms to help participants drive new business development, share knowledge, and explore new opportunities to address climate finance challenges in the Asia-Pacific region. The HKMA has also been actively supporting the development of green and sustainable finance in the region. In November 2020, the International Finance Corporation and the HKMA launched the "Green Commercial Banking Alliance" as a collaborative platform bringing together financial institutions, banking industry associations, research institutions, and technology solution providers in the region to jointly develop green commercial banking. Since March 2021, the Alliance has held 22 training events and roundtable discussions, attracting over 7,300 participants from the Asia-Pacific region, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Americas. In October, the Alliance jointly published with Crédit Agricole CIB the second thought leadership research report entitled "Developing Ambitious Green Banking Climate Strategies: Case Studies". During the year, the HKMA Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office joined the newly established "Coalition for Sustainable Investment Capacity Building" (CASI) and the "Green Investment and Financing Partnership" (GIFP) initiated by the Belt and Road Initiative Green Development Coalition. Collaboration with CASI and GIFP will facilitate capacity building and knowledge sharing, and channel more funds towards green and sustainable projects in Asia and beyond. In August 2023, GFANZ announced the establishment of its Hong Kong chapter, which will help support the net-zero commitments of Hong Kong and Mainland financial institutions. The HKMA serves in an advisory capacity to support GFANZ's work. To demonstrate the Government's commitment to addressing climate change, promoting green finance, and developing Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government launched the "Government Green Bond Programme" in 2018. The HKMA assists in the issuance of green bonds under the Programme. To date, the Government has issued approximately USD 25 billion equivalent of green institutional and retail bonds, with proceeds allocated to over 70 green government projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, energy efficiency and conservation. To enhance the transparency and accountability of the Programme, the Government publishes an annual Green Bond Report detailing the allocation of green bond proceeds and the expected environmental benefits. The Government continued its regular green institutional bond issuance in the 2023-24 financial year, issuing approximately USD 6 billion equivalent of green bonds in June. The tri-currency issuance covered bonds in US dollars, euros, and renminbi across various tenors, attracting a diverse range of investors and generating strong subscription interest, with orders totalling approximately USD 30 billion equivalent. The issuance size of the renminbi bonds was increased from RMB 10 billion issued in January to RMB 15 billion, and a 10-year renminbi bond was introduced for the first time, helping to extend the Government's renminbi yield curve and further enrich the range of offshore renminbi product offerings. The enthusiastic response from global investors to the Government's green bond issuance reflects investor recognition of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. In October, the Government issued the second tranche of green retail bonds with a total value of HKD 20 billion, further promoting market development and advancing financial inclusion. The issuance provided members of the public with an investment opportunity offering stable returns, allowing them to participate in and benefit from Hong Kong's green finance development.

As a major global asset owner and manager, the HKMA plays a pivotal role in advancing green and sustainable finance to support the global climate agenda. The HKMA has been a pioneer in responsible investment. Since 2015, the HKMA has been leading the way in investing in green and sustainable assets, requiring its external investment managers to actively exercise ownership rights and integrate environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors into the investment management of the Exchange Fund. Investing prudently in accordance with the principle of "preserving capital and achieving long-term growth,"¹ the HKMA believes that giving due consideration to ESG factors helps mitigate investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As one of the first central banks to sign the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI) and to set a "Net Zero by 2050" target² for its investment portfolio, the HKMA is committed to continuously advancing its responsible investment journey, with a focus on sustainability—particularly the pressing issue of climate change—with the aim of enhancing the resilience of the Exchange Fund and achieving better risk-adjusted long-term returns. As a responsible investor, the HKMA participates in building a robust green and sustainable finance ecosystem, working with like-minded investors, regulators and international organisations to establish industry practice standards and to promote the adoption of responsible investment across the financial sector and among central banks. Through stewardship and collaborative initiatives, the HKMA strives to foster a future where finance and sustainable development go hand in hand.  Figure 1: The Exchange Fund's Responsible Investment Journey  Comprehensive and reliable ESG information is critical to embedding sustainability and mapping out a credible climate transition pathway towards net zero. In fulfilment of its commitment to support the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) Glasgow Declaration³ and the strategic plan of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group, the HKMA practises what it preaches by preparing this chapter on the responsible investment of the Exchange Fund in accordance with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD).  The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee (EFAC), chaired by the Financial Secretary, sets the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office (EFIO) in managing the Exchange Fund's investments. The primary guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA in pursuing responsible investment while fulfilling the Exchange Fund's investment objectives. The Investment Committee under EFAC, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for monitoring ESG and climate-related risks associated with Exchange Fund investments. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management guidelines, and monitors implementation through regular reports from the EFIO's Sustainable Investment Team.  As illustrated in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the EFIO, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, is responsible for coordinating and overseeing the EFIO's ESG initiatives. Motions and work progress discussed at quarterly ESG Committee meetings are reported to the EFIO's Chief Executive Officer. In addition, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and attended by the EFIO's Chief Executive Officer and Chief Strategy Officer, meets semi-annually to provide guidance on ESG policies and measures across different HKMA functions, including the EFIO, in pursuit of the HKMA's overall ESG objectives.  Figure 2: The EFIO's Responsible Investment Governance Structure  As shown in Figure 1, the EFIO embarked on its responsible investment journey in 2016, with an initial focus on managing ESG risks that could affect the Exchange Fund's financial performance. As sustainable development evolved rapidly and moved beyond risk considerations to become a key strategic priority for major institutions globally, the EFIO revisited its approach to responsible investment. July 2023 marked another milestone, with the EFIO establishing a new Business Strategy department led by the Chief Strategy Officer, responsible for coordinating and leading the EFIO's strategic development, and incorporating the dedicated responsible investment team—formerly under the Risk Management and Monitoring department and now renamed the Sustainable Investment Team. This strategic realignment reflects the HKMA's elevation of the responsible investment focus from a risk-based approach to a more proactive and forward-looking stance in addressing sustainability-related investment matters.  The Sustainable Investment Team works closely with different teams within the EFIO on integrating ESG factors and assists senior EFIO staff in managing ESG—particularly climate-related—risks and opportunities across various investment portfolios:  Public Markets – The Credit, Compliance and Monitoring Committee, comprising senior EFIO staff, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models with input from the Sustainable Investment Team, and monitors the ESG status of the fixed income portfolio through periodic reports from the Risk Management and Monitoring department. The Sustainable Investment Team also participates from an ESG perspective in the selection, appointment and monitoring of external investment managers for the equity portfolio (see "Promoting Active Ownership" in the "Risk Management" section on page 40).  Private Markets – The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers ESG-related assessments made by the private markets investment and risk management teams for each investment proposal.  The HKMA recognises that the physical and transition risks⁴ arising from climate change, as well as the related opportunities, may affect the long-term performance and value of Exchange Fund investments. The United Nations Environment Programme's Emissions Gap Report 2023⁵ projects that global average temperatures will rise by 2.5 to 2.9 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels by 2030 unless further greenhouse gas emission reductions are made globally. The urgent need for more aggressive policies, technological development or behavioural change to limit temperature rise could amplify transition risks such as asset devaluation or stranded asset impacts. At the same time, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events also pose additional physical risks to investments.  The HKMA believes that investing in a greener future is aligned with the Exchange Fund's investment objectives, and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors in integrating ESG considerations. By setting a target in 2022 for the Exchange Fund's investment portfolio to achieve net zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, the HKMA has further demonstrated its commitment to the global climate agenda. The HKMA continues to strengthen its three-pronged approach with a clear focus on decarbonisation and transition. These approaches are described in detail in the sections below.  Figure 3: The HKMA's Three-Pronged Approach to Responsible Investment  In the journey towards net zero, the HKMA favours active engagement over exclusion or divestment from its investable universe. First, maintaining a diversified and resilient portfolio is crucial to achieving the Exchange Fund's primary investment objectives. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe and potentially affect investment returns and risk profiles. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA can seize opportunities to invest in companies that are undergoing transition and possess advanced technology and sound corporate governance to navigate evolving global climate trends—including companies in high-emission sectors. Second, addressing climate change requires the transition of core "brown" industries. Merely excluding related investments or divesting would not resolve the issue of carbon emissions. Instead, by deploying strategic capital and exercising active ownership to support these industries, the HKMA encourages them to adopt sustainable and low-carbon operating practices, thereby bringing about positive change both for themselves and for the world at large.  In response to market developments, the HKMA is refining its net zero investment strategy with a comprehensive approach to achieve transition outcomes aligned with the Exchange Fund's and global net zero objectives, while adhering to its guiding principles for responsible investment. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to seek sustainable investments and opportunities that advance climate transition and enhance the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund's portfolio (Figure 4).  The HKMA's responsible investment maintained strong momentum in 2023. In public markets, the HKMA launched a new active global equity portfolio themed around sustainability and climate transition, managed by external investment managers, and expanded the application of customised low-carbon equity indices to another portfolio managed by external investment managers. In addition, the HKMA's prioritised investments in green, social and sustainability bonds outperformed the investment benchmark, demonstrating the concept of "doing good while doing well." In private markets, the HKMA is actively building a resilient long-term growth portfolio by capturing investment opportunities expected to benefit from long-term economic trends such as the climate and energy transition. For example, during the year, the HKMA invested in two Asia-focused transition investment funds, reflecting its commitment to addressing Asia's climate transition needs.  Figure 4: Continued Implementation of Measures to Promote ESG Investment  The HKMA has invested in a company that specialises in producing eco-friendly thermoplastic materials from unsorted household waste—including organic matter such as food waste—and non-recyclable materials. Unlike conventional chemical recycling systems that rely on energy-intensive high-temperature environments to produce plastics, this company has pioneered a low-temperature production method powered entirely by solar arrays. This 100% waste-derived plastic material serves as a substitute for oil-based resins commonly used in industries such as retail and consumer durables, offering a sustainable and versatile alternative. At the same time, this plastic material is compatible with existing standard manufacturing processes and cutting-edge technologies such as 3D printing. The company is firmly committed to supporting the circular economy. The following diagram illustrates the positive environmental outcomes of its advanced plastic production process.  The Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Programme (MCPP), managed by the International Finance Corporation (IFC), is an innovative initiative that combines institutional investors' capital with the IFC's own funds to scale up sustainable financing for private companies in emerging markets. The HKMA committed USD 1 billion in each of two tranches to the MCPP in 2017 and 2019, and further collaborated with the IFC to create a new global climate-related investment platform, "MCPP One Planet," in 2021—the world's first cross-sector emerging market loan portfolio aligned with the Paris Agreement. Through the MCPP programme, the HKMA has committed to providing loans to 80 sustainable development projects across 19 sectors, including infrastructure, agriculture, real estate and manufacturing, in 38 developing countries.  The IFC has collected data on MCPP loans. According to IFC reports, the HKMA's loan commitments have provided support to emerging markets and developing countries across various areas, including economic transition and human resources development. Specifically, the projects receiving the HKMA's loans are expected to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by approximately 5.6 million tonnes of CO₂ equivalent annually, which is equivalent to the greenhouse gas emissions from driving a typical petrol-powered car for 14 billion miles. The HKMA actively collaborates with like-minded investors and partners to advance responsible investment and enhance industry capacity.

The HKMA is committed to becoming a sustainable institution, adopting a multi-pronged approach to reducing its carbon footprint, with a target of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA places emphasis on employee well-being and social responsibility, and strives to advance financial inclusion and enhance the public's financial literacy. As a responsible institution, the HKMA sets sustainability targets under three pillars: environment, people, and social responsibility. The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee)¹, established in October and chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, serves as the principal decision-making body for institutional sustainability initiatives. The Steering Committee succeeds the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainable Development Committee, which was responsible for leading the HKMA in formulating its vision, strategy, and policies on institutional sustainability and social responsibility matters. At the departmental level, the Executive Director (Corporate Development and Operations) oversees the implementation of sustainability activities and submits regular progress reports to the Steering Committee. The Green Office Task Force and the Volunteer Services Team provide support for coordinating institutional sustainability efforts; the former serves as a platform for brainstorming ideas on how to create a green working environment, while the latter aims to cultivate a culture of volunteering. The HKMA has developed a roadmap to guide its transition pathway. Key priorities include implementing decarbonisation strategies in its day-to-day operations, encompassing the operation of green buildings and data centres, the adoption of green travel practices, energy-saving measures, digital tools and greener operating practices, waste reduction, and the fostering of a sustainability culture. The HKMA also plans to apply carbon-embedding tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions, and to adopt carbon offsetting measures for emissions that are difficult to reduce. Beyond the environmental commitments relating to its day-to-day operations, the HKMA continues to introduce greener operational solutions for the wider community, ranging from channels for banks to submit electronic documents and maintain liaison, to electronic payment and coin collection programmes for the general public. To strengthen and sustain its operational capabilities, the HKMA employs a team of professionals, builds up its talent pool, and pays close attention to staff well-being. In terms of social responsibility, the HKMA encourages employees to participate in volunteer and charitable activities; considers procuring from social enterprises (SEs); promotes financial consumer education; and works with the banking industry to ensure that basic banking services are fairly accessible to all sectors of the community. The remainder of this chapter sets out the details of each of these strategies.  Under the HKMA's overall institutional risk management framework, the Risk Committee², chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the potential risks and threats that the HKMA faces in its day-to-day operations, including those arising from climate change. The physical impacts of climate change, such as flooding or other damage caused by more frequent extreme weather events, may affect the HKMA's offices and impede employees' ability to commute. To manage physical risks, the HKMA regularly updates its business continuity plan to address extreme weather conditions. The HKMA also conducts regular evacuation and backup facility activation drills to ensure that staff are at all times prepared to execute business continuity measures. A number of measures have also been incorporated into the design of its offices to mitigate potential risks. Transition risks may affect the HKMA's energy use, air travel, and waste disposal. The HKMA has been monitoring its transition risk exposure by tracking its own greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, energy consumption, and paper usage.  The HKMA's climate target is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions across Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 (air travel) in all areas of institutional operations by 2050 or earlier. As near-term emission reduction targets, the HKMA plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions by converting all of its existing vehicles to electric vehicles, and to reduce Scope 2 emission intensity by 63% by 2030 or earlier using 2015 as the base year, through a combination of decarbonisation and offsetting strategies. Despite the challenges in quantifying Scope 3 emissions, the HKMA will take a multi-pronged approach to the extent practicable to minimise Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions (such as those from paper use, waste generation, and air travel). The HKMA's long-term and near-term emission reduction targets were formulated with reference to the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) methodology, which has been verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA). The HKMA has commissioned the HKQAA to verify the emissions, energy consumption and paper usage, and waste data disclosed in this report⁶. The scope and basis of verification are set out in the "Verification Statement" section of this report.  In 2023, in addition to publishing the 2022 Annual Report, the HKMA published its first standalone 2022 Sustainability Report. The HKMA's enhanced ESG reporting was recognised with an ESG award in the "Public Sector Category" at the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants' "Best Corporate Governance and ESG Awards 2023". The HKMA is the first financial regulator to receive an award in this category. The judging panel commended the HKMA for meeting high ESG standards, for the clarity and readability of its Sustainability Report, and for commissioning an independent body to verify its target-setting methodology and the environmental data disclosed in the report, reflecting its commitment to reporting with a high degree of transparency and accountability. In addition, the HKMA received the highest rating of gold award in the "Non-Profit and Charitable Organisation" category at the Hong Kong Management Association's "Best Annual Reports 2023". The judging panel commended the HKMA's annual report for its clear presentation of comprehensive financial information and effective use of infographics, demonstrating the HKMA's commitment to enhancing financial literacy and promoting financial inclusion. In recognition of the HKMA's dedication to caring for the environment, its employees, and society as a whole, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the HKMA the "15 Years+" Caring Organisation Logo for 17 consecutive years since 2006.  The HKMA is committed to properly managing the environmental impact of its operations. Its internal Green Office Guidelines provide employees with guidance on resource use and office waste generation. The HKMA has incorporated environmental considerations into the design, operation, and maintenance of its owned and leased offices. When renovating offices, existing furniture and fitting materials are reused wherever possible to reduce waste, and priority is given to environmentally friendly construction and decorative materials. The HKMA has consistently followed this approach, which led to its partially renovated offices at Two International Finance Centre receiving Gold-level certification under both LEED⁷ and BEAM Plus Interior Building Assessment⁸ in 2021 and 2022 respectively.  Leveraging new technologies and making better use of existing technologies to improve energy efficiency remains one of the HKMA's key areas of focus. In addition to promoting good practices such as switching off unnecessary lighting in the work area outside office hours to save electricity, other energy-saving measures include the use of LED lighting, motion sensors, setting the air-conditioning temperature at an appropriate level, and making efficient use of energy in IT network infrastructure. The HKMA's energy consumption has continued to decline, reaching 2.59 MWh per capita in 2023⁹, a decrease of 29.7% from the 2015 baseline (Figure 1).  Given the nature of the HKMA's day-to-day operations, its greenhouse gas emissions primarily arise from the consumption of electricity generated from fossil fuels.
