In 2023, the combined Scope 1 and Scope 2 emission intensity from purchased fuel and electricity was 1.48 tCO₂e per capita¹⁰, a reduction of 45.2% compared with 2015 (Figure 2).  In addition to standardised equipment, office software, and conferencing facilities, the HKMA employs digital tools and technologies, automates and streamlines workflows, builds a digitalised working environment, and enhances online collaboration within the institution.¹¹ Paperless meetings have become the HKMA's primary mode of conducting meetings. To further reduce paper consumption and improve efficiency, internal administrative processes are predominantly conducted through electronic procedures. Furthermore, the HKMA encourages employees to embrace green and digitalised working practices, replacing paper documents and communications with digital alternatives. Meanwhile, the implementation of an electronic records management system is ongoing.  These green and digitalisation measures have yielded positive results. The HKMA's paper consumption intensity in 2023 was 11.55 kg per capita, a substantial reduction of 64.8% compared with 2015 (Figure 3).  As most international events have returned to in-person format following the COVID-19 pandemic, and as it is necessary to advance Hong Kong's status as an international financial centre, overseas business travel by relevant HKMA staff is unavoidable. To reduce the carbon emissions associated with air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to take direct flights or to combine different business trips where practicable when attending overseas events. At the institutional level, in 2023 the HKMA reduced its Scope 3 emissions by 126 tCO₂e through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel. In addition, the HKMA participates in a "Gold Standard"¹² certified carbon offset programme to offset the remaining carbon emissions from air travel; the programme carries out waste-to-energy, solar power generation, and the provision of more efficient and cleaner cooking facilities in developing countries. The HKMA will continue to make similar arrangements in 2024.  The HKMA's procurement process takes sustainability and environmental considerations into account. As part of a comprehensive review of the institution's procurement policies and procedures, the existing practice of procuring green products has been formalised, ensuring compliance with the environmental specifications of the Government's "Green Procurement List", particularly in the procurement of electrical appliances and office consumables. In addition, ESG factors and innovative proposals that contribute to productivity and efficiency improvements have been incorporated into tender evaluation criteria. Moreover, all suppliers are required to commit to complying with environmental regulations.  In accordance with the "4R" principles of Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle, the HKMA takes a three-pronged approach to minimising waste generation and managing waste disposal. Furthermore, the HKMA conducted two waste audits in 2022 and 2023 to assist in formulating targeted waste management strategies. Details of non-hazardous waste generated, including general waste sent to landfills and various types of recyclable waste, are provided in the "Performance Summary" section on page 56.  In 2023, the HKMA participated for the first time directly in the lai see envelope recycling programme organised by the building management company of the International Finance Centre office tower. Employees submitted approximately 3,000 used but still pristine lai see envelopes, which were subsequently passed to an environmental organisation for distribution to the public for use during the following Lunar New Year.  Given that the HKMA's operational and backup data centres account for a significant portion of the institution's overall energy consumption, both data centres have been upgraded to meet the highest standards set by BEAM Plus for existing data centres, achieving optimal Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE)¹³. In 2023, the HKMA's two data centres received "Gold" and "Platinum" ratings respectively under the "BEAM Plus Existing Data Centres" assessment criteria issued in 2021; the HKMA is the first and only institution in Hong Kong to receive such ratings. Improving the energy efficiency of the two data centres has long been a key focus of the technology team. To this end, the team incorporated green design principles in renovation works and adopted energy-efficient best practices to lower PUE and achieve the relevant targets, including round-the-clock monitoring of the data centres' environmental facilities and continuous improvements to environmental factors such as airflow and temperature settings. As the technology team continued to improve energy utilisation in the data centres, the HKMA commissioned an external consultant in December 2021 to conduct a review to comprehensively assess the green performance of the data centres and to formulate recommendations for further performance enhancements. The study was completed in mid-2022. Shortly after the study's completion, the HKMA began preparing to obtain "Green Data Centre" certification under the BEAM Plus certification programme. The certification process is comprehensive and rigorous. Throughout 2023, the technology team introduced optimisation measures in accordance with the recommendations of the consultant's report, enhancing energy performance as well as health-related aspects of the working environment within the data centres.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) conducted an independent verification of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (HKMA) 2023 Environmental Data (the "2023 Data"). The 2023 Data encompasses the total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, business air travel GHG emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfills and recyclable waste) for the year 2023, together with their respective intensities and changes compared to 2015 levels. In addition, the 2023 Data includes the amount of food waste generated during the year, its intensity, and the change compared to the level at the time when the HKMA launched its food waste recycling programme in November 2022. The HKMA's GHG emissions data were prepared in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (GHG Protocol) jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The verification scope covers the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2023, as well as the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 used for annual performance comparison (except food waste). The verification scope covers a total of 5 office and warehouse assets, comprising 4 offices located at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) Pacific Place One, and 4) Landmark East, and a warehouse at 5) Loksun Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance on the accuracy and reliability of the 2023 Data, and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanisms. Within the verification scope, HKQAA reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from the 5 assets. The verification was conducted in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised) – "Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and conclusion in order to achieve a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was defined in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing selected sample data back to their sources, and examined and tested the reliability of the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation and internal review. The verification process also included verifying internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with representatives responsible for preparing the 2023 Data, and selecting representative data and information for examination. The relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for data collection and reporting. Our verification work was conducted with complete independence and impartiality. The HKQAA verification team had no involvement in the preparation of the 2023 Data. Based on the results of this verification, HKQAA provides reasonable assurance on the 2023 Data and concludes that: the 2023 Data are materially accurate and reliable; and the HKMA's overall data collection mechanisms are adequate.  Shen Xiaoyin Verification Manager Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency April 2024

The threat posed by climate change is increasingly urgent, making it imperative to accelerate global climate action. The World Meteorological Organization has confirmed that 2024 was the hottest year on record and the first year in which global temperatures exceeded the critical threshold of 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Meanwhile, global greenhouse gas emissions, which had briefly moderated during the COVID-19 pandemic, have recently reached new highs, underscoring the inadequacy of current climate mitigation measures. As the world grapples with global warming, the materialisation of climate-related risks is set to intensify, with unpredictable consequences for economies and financial markets. Compounding these challenges are heightened geopolitical tensions, an increasingly fragmented global economic landscape, aggravated energy security concerns, and an uncertain economic outlook, all of which make it harder for countries to address climate change. The transition to a low-carbon economy requires substantial and sustained financial support. Across the globe, Asia in particular faces the most daunting transition challenges. As the World Economic Forum has noted, Asia is not only the engine of global economic growth, but also the region most vulnerable to the impacts of climate change. Asia therefore plays a pivotal role in determining whether the world can successfully achieve net-zero emissions. As Asia's leading international financial centre, Hong Kong has a responsibility to strengthen its leadership role and harness the power of finance to support and drive the region's transition. To this end, the HKMA published its Sustainable Finance Action Agenda last year, setting out our vision and roadmap for progressively embedding sustainability into the core of the financial system. Our work focuses both on strengthening the financial sector's capacity to manage climate-related risks and on helping the industry seize the new opportunities that arise from the transition. At the same time, we lead by example. The HKMA's sustainability work encompasses four key areas: supporting the banking sector on its path to net zero, investing in a sustainable future, facilitating net-zero financing, and promoting more inclusive sustainable development. The banking sector plays a critical role in Hong Kong's and Asia's net-zero transition, yet it also faces considerable risks in the process. In the Action Agenda, we have set ambitious targets, requiring all banks to commit to achieving net-zero emissions in their own operations by 2030 or earlier, and net-zero financed emissions by 2050 or earlier. We also require all banks to enhance disclosure of climate-related risks and opportunities. While continuing to strengthen banks' climate risk management, we are providing guidance on transition planning to help them build transition resilience and better manage the associated risks. We are also working with relevant stakeholders to prepare for aligning Hong Kong's sustainable disclosure requirements with international standards, with the aim of further enhancing transparency in the sector. In addition, we are refining the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance, launched in May last year, to incorporate a broader range of sustainable activities, including transition activities. By providing clear criteria, we hope to channel more capital towards sustainable and transition-related projects. Climate change gives rise to significant physical and transition risks that could affect the long-term financial performance and value of Exchange Fund investments. At the same time, it also presents opportunities for the Exchange Fund to generate growth and deliver positive impact. Our experience has demonstrated that investment returns and positive sustainable impact are complementary rather than conflicting. With this in mind, we are committed to achieving net-zero emissions across the Exchange Fund's investment portfolio by 2050 or earlier, and have pledged in the Action Agenda to support Asia's climate transition through Exchange Fund investments. Currently, sustainable investments account for more than 10% of the portfolio. To further promote sustainable investment in the region, the HKMA established strategic partnerships in November last year with the Asian Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, and the International Finance Corporation, with the aim of accelerating Asia's low-carbon economic transition through co-investment. In addition, we published our inaugural HKMA ESG Expectations document in September last year to further encourage fund managers to exercise active stewardship and adopt sound sustainable investment practices. The mobilisation of capital is particularly crucial to accelerating the regional transition. As an international financial hub and the preferred location for Asian issuers — including Mainland provincial and municipal governments — to arrange international sustainable bond issuances, Hong Kong plays an important role in directing capital to accelerate the regional transition. The Action Agenda sets out the vision for developing Hong Kong into the region's preferred sustainable finance platform, as well as the goal of fostering sustainable finance innovation. From leveraging the demonstration effect of the Government Green Bond Programme to drive green bond innovation — including the world's first multi-currency digital green bonds issued in February last year — to expanding the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme in May last year to cover transition finance instruments, and to the launch of the Digital Bond Grant Scheme in November last year, we have been steadfastly encouraging regional issuers to use Hong Kong's financial platform to raise the capital needed for their low-carbon transitions. Achieving an orderly transition requires not only capital and innovation, but also an inclusive and accessible sustainability ecosystem. This encompasses reliable sustainability data, highly transparent disclosure, and industry professionals equipped with the relevant knowledge and skills. In this regard, the Action Agenda includes commitments to support high-quality and comprehensive sustainable disclosure, and to address the gap in sustainable finance talent and knowledge in the region. We have made good progress in assisting stakeholders and facilitating sustainable disclosure, in particular by providing accessible climate disclosure templates to facilitate small and medium-sized enterprises' sustainability reporting. We also launched the Green and Sustainable Finance professional module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners in November last year, to deepen the knowledge and skills of banking practitioners in Hong Kong. Furthermore, through the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week in February last year and other events, we have engaged stakeholders in sustainability discussions to foster collaboration and innovation. Within the HKMA itself, we are committed to ensuring that our operations are aligned with our sustainability vision. In the Action Agenda, we pledged to achieve net-zero emissions in our own operations by 2030 or earlier — 20 years ahead of our original commitment. We are also actively preparing to meet international sustainable disclosure standards in accordance with the government-issued roadmap. We began adopting electric vehicles in 2024 and have incorporated low carbon emissions as a screening criterion in our procurement process. We continue to improve operational efficiency through digitalisation, cultivate a culture of sustainability within the organisation, and encourage staff to actively participate in sustainability efforts. Multilateral cooperation has long been the cornerstone of global efforts to address climate change, but the reshaping of the international order and dramatic shifts in the geopolitical landscape have introduced new uncertainties into global climate action. Nevertheless, climate change is an undeniable reality that is progressively intensifying. The current situation leaves no room for complacency in our work on addressing climate change. We firmly believe that advancing an orderly and inclusive transition will help mitigate the impact of climate risks on Hong Kong's financial system, while creating opportunities along the way. As we move into 2025, we will press forward with determination in advancing our sustainability agenda and deepening our relationships with like-minded partners. Despite the formidable challenges ahead, we will remain steadfast in our commitment to supporting Hong Kong, Asia, and beyond in building a sustainable future.

Climate change is one of the defining challenges of our time. As an international financial centre and a sustainable finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong is committed to playing a pioneering role in supporting sustainable development across Asia and beyond. In October 2024, the HKMA published its Sustainable Finance Action Plan (the "Action Plan"), setting out the HKMA's vision in this area, including our future direction, a timeline for achieving various targets, and how we expect the industry to work together to advance the relevant efforts. The HKMA plans to strengthen the financial sector's and its own capacity to manage climate-related risks, and to drive Asia's transition to a more sustainable economy, through formulating strategic policies, enhancing regulatory engagement, and improving internal operations. By actively participating in international and regional discussions, the HKMA also seeks to exercise influence in shaping green and sustainable finance policies and standards at the regional and global levels. As a banking regulator, the HKMA focuses on enhancing the climate resilience of the banking sector and supporting banks in remaining safe and sound as they transition to net-zero. Our key priorities in 2025 include:  - Conducting a new round of thematic examinations on banks' climate risk management practices, along with a third round of consultation meetings, to review banks' implementation of the HKMA's relevant supervisory requirements and to further strengthen banks' climate risk management capabilities; - Finalising the incorporation of climate risk stress testing into the HKMA's regulator-led stress testing framework; - Continuing to advance the integration of climate factors into the HKMA's Supervisory Review Process; - Commencing preparatory work for implementing the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's forthcoming Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks and the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards) for the local banking sector; - Completing the drafting of a new module GS-2 of the Supervisory Policy Manual to provide guidance to banks on transition planning; and - Sharing good practices on climate risk management and the application of green fintech with the industry.  Beyond its role as a banking regulator, the HKMA also acts as a facilitator, dedicated to fostering the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem and supporting banks in financing the transition. We have published Phase 1 of the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance, providing the industry with a tool for identifying green and sustainable economic activities and facilitating related financing. The HKMA has commenced Phase 2 of the Taxonomy to expand its coverage, including the incorporation of transition elements, the addition of more green economic activities, and the inclusion of climate adaptation objectives. In addition, building on the success of the 3rd FiNETech event in 2024 and the Green Fintech Competition in 2023, we will organise another green fintech event in 2025 to encourage banks to adopt green fintech solutions.  Hong Kong is well-positioned to support the region's sustainable financing needs. To reinforce this role, we will continue to assist the Government in implementing the Government Sustainable Bond Programme, the expanded scope of which will cover sustainable projects, including social projects. This will help deepen the development of the local green and sustainable bond market and serve as a demonstration for other potential issuers in the region. We will also continue to provide subsidies through the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme to encourage more regional borrowers to use Hong Kong's financing platform to raise sustainable funds. We will step up our promotional efforts to encourage more Mainland and overseas governments, institutions, and corporates to raise green capital in Hong Kong. At the same time, we will continue to catalyse and support sustainable finance innovation, including by providing subsidies to prospective issuers of digital green bonds through the Digital Bond Grant Scheme.  While the demand for high-quality sustainability disclosures from institutions and corporates is growing, different entities vary in their capacity and readiness to make such disclosures, and some may require additional guidance and support. With this in mind, the HKMA will continue to work with other members of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group to make sustainability disclosures more accessible and inclusive. For example, we will continue to provide banks and their clients with a richer suite of climate disclosure-related tools, including user-friendly sustainability disclosure templates and complementary tools; explore how technology can be leveraged to make existing resources even more accessible; and collaborate with major local industry associations to deliver the training that the industry needs.  The sustainable finance market is evolving rapidly, necessitating an expansion of the local talent pool and the bridging of knowledge gaps in Hong Kong and across the region. The HKMA's key work in 2025 includes collaborating with the banking industry to develop professional-level training programmes for the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the Banking Professional Qualification Framework, and identifying areas requiring further training through the forthcoming Future Talent in Banking 2026–2030 study. We also plan to work with key stakeholders to enhance the promotion of the Government-funded Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Programme and to review its scope of application. At the regional level, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with the International Finance Corporation through the Green Commercial Banking Alliance to roll out dedicated initiatives in Asia, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market insights, offering targeted upskilling and training support, fostering community connections, facilitating potential green investment opportunities, and providing practical guidance to help banks develop roadmaps for growing green finance as a core business.  As a responsible investor, the HKMA is committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's Investment Portfolio by 2050 or earlier in support of the broader economic transition. We will continue to enhance the sustainability of the Exchange Fund's investments through a pragmatic and rigorous responsible investment approach, with a primary focus on the long-term resilience of the portfolio while exploring investment opportunities that can promote positive climate outcomes.  The HKMA is committed to leading by example in its institutional sustainability efforts. In response to the accelerated net-zero commitment timeline announced in the Action Plan, the HKMA will progressively incorporate environmental and social factors into its strategy, risk assessment, and reporting at a pragmatic pace to continue driving institutional sustainability. Specifically, in 2025 we will conduct a double materiality assessment to deepen our understanding of the potential financial and non-financial impacts of climate change and other sustainability issues, ensuring that we remain focused on material matters. We will also conduct an energy audit and utilise technology solutions to assess the material impacts of climate risks on our offices and operations, so as to enhance our climate resilience and risk preparedness. We support the Government's publication of the Hong Kong Sustainable Disclosure Roadmap and are actively preparing to make disclosures in accordance with the ISSB Standards. In 2025, the HKMA will continue to honour its commitment to applying energy efficiency and conservation principles in the selection of data centres for planned upgrade projects. We will also expand digital initiatives to promote sustainability and improve efficiency, including developing digital tools and platforms to support paperless processes and waste reduction, and enhancing the overall digital experience for our staff, banks, and the general public.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impacts. Through its multiple roles as a monetary authority, banking regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor, and sustainable institution, the HKMA contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across Asia. The HKMA has in place a robust sustainability governance framework to lead the formulation of its sustainability-related strategies and policies, oversee the implementation of related measures, and ensure that sustainability factors are incorporated into the HKMA's own operations and working practices. In its commitment to sound institutional governance, the HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework with clear accountability arrangements and a high degree of transparency for its sustainability-related work. This governance framework ensures that sustainability factors are effectively integrated into the HKMA's strategic planning and decision-making processes, and that effective mechanisms are in place to monitor and assess the progress and effectiveness of sustainability work.  The HKMA's sustainability governance framework comprises: - The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its dedicated sub-committees, which oversee the HKMA's work, including its sustainability work, and provide recommendations; - The Green and Sustainable Finance Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which leads the HKMA's overall Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) strategies and policies at the management level; - In respect of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, which coordinates and oversees ESG-related work within the Exchange Fund Investment Office; and - In respect of other functional areas, relevant teams and working groups, which plan and implement sustainability-related measures covering banking and market development as well as the HKMA's own operations.  At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), co-initiated by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the work of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders, and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong.  In view of the significant expansion in the scope of the HKMA's sustainability work over the past years, the Steering Committee was established in October 2023 as a central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability-related work across the HKMA's different functional areas. Its responsibilities include: - Providing guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies, and plans for ESG-related matters across four functional areas: banking, development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, Exchange Fund investments, and internal operations; - Overseeing the implementation of ESG-related initiatives by the HKMA's functional departments; - Assessing the HKMA's performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and - Overseeing external communications strategies.  The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with the three Deputy Chief Executives serving as permanent members. In addition, Assistant Chief Executives responsible for key functional areas related to green and sustainable development matters are invited to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on key outcomes and future plans for their respective work. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA's Banking Department, Corporate Development and Operations Department, External Affairs Department, and Exchange Fund Investment Office.  In addition to developing and implementing its own sustainability measures, the HKMA co-initiated the Steering Group with the SFC in May 2020. The Steering Group serves as a cross-agency platform to provide strategic direction and coordinate cross-sectoral work on the financial industry's response to climate and environmental risks, with a view to consolidating Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in Asia and globally. For details on the work of the Steering Group, please refer to the chapter on "Advancing the Development of the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem".

Climate change can pose risks to the financial system. The HKMA has been committed to strengthening the Hong Kong financial system's resilience to climate risks, while contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks are exposed to a wide range of sustainability and climate-related matters in their day-to-day operations and must therefore proactively manage climate risks. At the same time, banks play a pivotal role in the financial system by channelling funds towards green and sustainable projects. As the banking regulator, the HKMA places particular emphasis on building banks' capacity to address and manage climate risks, and on accelerating banks' efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. In October, the HKMA published its Sustainable Finance Action Agenda (Action Agenda), setting out its vision to further consolidate Hong Kong's position as a regional sustainable finance hub and to support sustainable development across Asia and globally. The Action Agenda comprises eight objectives under four pillars. To assist the industry in meeting the objectives of the relevant banking policy, we have been undertaking the following initiatives.  All banks committed to achieving net-zero operational emissions by 2030 or earlier, and net-zero financed emissions by 2050 or earlier. All banks increased the transparency of climate-related risks and opportunities. In December, the HKMA shared good practices in transition planning with the industry and launched an industry consultation on the draft Supervisory Policy Manual (SPM) module GS-2 on "Transition Planning". The new module is intended to provide guidance on enhancing banks' capabilities in addressing net-zero transition and related risk management. In addition, we are reviewing the Supervisory Review Process used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy levels and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with the aim of incorporating relevant factors set out by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (Basel Committee) on the effective management of climate-related financial risks into the assessment process, and encouraging banks to enhance their risk management frameworks (including transition planning) to address climate risks.  The HKMA has been committed to aligning local sustainable disclosure requirements with international standards, including the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards) and the Basel Committee's Pillar 3 disclosure framework on climate-related financial risks. Specifically, the HKMA is analysing the latest developments in sustainable disclosure and supporting the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants in conducting a technical feasibility study on the adoption of ISSB Standards.  Promoting green and transition finance is central to the implementation of the Action Agenda. In May, the HKMA published the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance (the Taxonomy) to address industry concerns about greenwashing and to help guide capital flows towards green and sustainable activities. The Taxonomy covers 12 economic activities across four sectors, and is designed to align with the Common Ground Taxonomy and the taxonomies of Mainland China and the European Union, while also incorporating locally relevant elements. We have commenced Phase 2 work to expand the coverage of the Taxonomy and are consulting a wide range of stakeholders to further facilitate the flow of green and sustainable capital.  During the year, the HKMA further strengthened its supervision of banks' climate risk management and worked to support banks in building their capacity to manage climate-related risks and opportunities and to respond to climate change. The HKMA also completed all work under the two-year plan established in 2022 to integrate climate risks into the banking supervisory process.  To promote banks' ability to enhance climate risk management, the HKMA shared with the banking industry good practices observed during thematic reviews and consultation meetings, covering key areas including:  - Establishing robust governance frameworks with clearly defined responsibilities for the Board and senior management; and - Ensuring effective oversight of key aspects of climate-related risk matters, namely:   (1) facilitating and monitoring the effective formulation and implementation of climate strategies;   (2) exercising appropriate oversight of climate-related risk management; and   (3) fostering a sound climate risk culture within the institution.  The HKMA hosted a Balanced Regulation Roundtable in August themed on climate risk management. At the roundtable, bank representatives and HKMA participants exchanged views on a range of climate risk-related topics, including the challenges banks face in climate risk management, climate risk stress testing, transition planning, and financing. The roundtable provided an interactive platform for information sharing and contributed to the HKMA's work on climate risk supervision and other related matters.  The HKMA conducted a round of thematic reviews on banks' climate risk management frameworks and practices, assessing their robustness and adequacy against the supervisory expectations set out in SPM module GS-1 on "Climate Risk Management". The thematic reviews covered the full risk management process, including risk identification, measurement, monitoring, reporting, control and mitigation, as well as climate risk scenario analysis and stress testing.  The HKMA held a second series of consultation meetings to assess the progress of a new cohort of banks in implementing SPM module GS-1 on "Climate Risk Management" and to understand the challenges they face. The consultation meetings also covered the latest regulatory and market developments in climate-related areas, including transition planning, disclosure frameworks and standards, and greenwashing issues. We provided feedback and guidance tailored to individual banks' circumstances to support their climate risk management efforts.  The HKMA completed the second round of the Banking Sector Climate Risk Stress Test (CRST) in 2024, with the participation of 21 retail banks and the Hong Kong branches of 25 international banking groups. The results demonstrated that Hong Kong's banking sector continues to exhibit strong resilience against severe climate-related shocks under various scenarios, including those assuming the simultaneous occurrence of climate risks and macroeconomic downturns. Compared with the CRST pilot exercise, participating banks significantly enhanced their capabilities in measuring and assessing climate risks. A report presenting the CRST results and the good practices observed by the HKMA during the process was published in February 2025.  Recognising the numerous data and methodological challenges banks face in climate risk management, the HKMA has been pursuing a range of initiatives to facilitate the application of technology to address these challenges. To tackle the lack of physical risk-related data and analytical tools for climate risk assessment, the HKMA launched a Physical Risk Assessment Platform in May, enabling banks to assess the potential impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios. Going forward, the HKMA will enhance the platform by incorporating user feedback and additional local data.  In addition, the HKMA worked with relevant stakeholders to promote the adoption of green fintech solutions by banks and the broader financial services industry. During the year, we published an application practice guide and two Regtech Use Case Briefs (English versions) illustrating technology solutions for ESG and sustainability assessments as well as greenwashing risk management. We also hosted the third edition of "FiNETech", bringing together over 150 financial institutions and technology companies to explore green fintech collaboration.  Recognising the potential risks that climate change may pose to the financial system, the HKMA has incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risk analysis and research to strengthen ongoing monitoring. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks and includes analysis of climate-related risks in various financial stability reports.  Through active participation in the scenario design and analysis workstream under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA helped further enrich climate scenarios that assist central banks and supervisors in understanding the macroeconomic and financial implications of climate change. In November, the NGFS published the fifth vintage of its long-term climate macro-financial scenarios, providing a reference for forward-looking climate risk assessment.  As a member of the Financial Stability Board's (FSB) workstream on transition planning, the HKMA participated in the analysis of the interplay between transition plans of financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, enabling policymakers to examine climate-related financial risks from a forward-looking and dynamic perspective.  The HKMA published a "Practical Guide on Application of Green Technology by Banks" (English version), providing financial institutions with best practices for leveraging green technology to facilitate their net-zero transition.  On the research front, the HKMA undertook a number of applied research projects exploring the impact of climate change on the financial industry and the broader economy. Research topics included the cross-border transmission of climate transition risks, the role of firms' environmental performance in absorbing monetary policy shocks, the impact of climate-related factors on foreign direct investment flows, and the role of the financial sector in the transition to a low-carbon economy. These research findings not only deepen our understanding of how climate change affects financial stability, but also provide valuable insights into the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, thereby informing related policy formulation. Domestically, the research helps strengthen the HKMA's ongoing monitoring and assessment of climate change's impact on financial stability. The findings are also shared with a broad range of stakeholders through international forums and various channels such as the HKMA Research Memoranda.  The Hong Kong Institute for Monetary and Financial Research (HKIMR), the research arm of the Academy of Finance, published a research paper on the impact of carbon pricing on corporate performance. The study provides evidence that low-emission firms can derive significant benefits from carbon pricing and highlights its role in improving efficiency by reallocating resources from high-emission to low-emission firms. The research was featured in the HKIMR's Insights from Monetary Research and shared with local and international academics and policy researchers.  The HKMA's Liquidity Facilities Framework is a collateralised contingent funding arrangement providing timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework.  The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through such engagement, we help facilitate international and regional policy dialogue on addressing climate change and its implications for financial stability, and draw on lessons learned to help strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong's financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the HKMA is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and enablers, and supporting relevant international initiatives to align with global standards. As set out in the HKMA's Sustainable Finance Action Agenda ("Action Agenda"), the HKMA is dedicated to enhancing the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by driving net-zero financing and fostering more inclusive sustainable development. Specifically, we are committed to positioning Hong Kong as the preferred sustainable financing platform for borrowers in the region and globally, supporting technology and innovation in the green segment of financial markets, enhancing sustainable disclosure in the industry, expanding the local green talent pool, and addressing knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in Hong Kong and the region.  **Positioning Hong Kong as the Preferred Sustainable Financing Platform in the Region and Globally** **Catalysing Sustainable Finance Innovation** **Supporting High-quality and Comprehensive Sustainable Disclosure** **Bridging the Talent and Knowledge Gap in Sustainable Finance in the Region**  To demonstrate the Government's commitment to addressing climate change, promoting green finance, and developing Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government launched the Government Green Bond Programme in 2018. To date, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing approximately USD 28 billion equivalent in green bonds, sold to institutional and retail investors. The proceeds raised have been allocated to over 110 Government green projects, covering areas such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, energy efficiency and conservation, among others. We have seized every issuance opportunity to innovate and expand the features of green bonds, including currencies, tenors and distribution channels, laying the groundwork for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. In 2024, to enhance the impact of the programme and further strengthen Hong Kong's position as a green and sustainable finance hub, the programme's scope was expanded to cover sustainable projects and was renamed the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme" (Sustainable Bond Programme).  To enhance the transparency and accountability of the Sustainable Bond Programme, the Government publishes an annual Green Bond Report detailing the allocation of green bond proceeds and expected environmental benefits. In July, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing approximately USD 3 billion equivalent in institutional green bonds under the Sustainable Bond Programme. The triple-currency issuance covered bonds denominated in RMB, USD and EUR across different tenors. The bonds attracted strong participation from a diverse range of investors, with total subscriptions reaching over USD 15 billion equivalent. Among the issuances, the 20-year and 30-year RMB green bonds were the Government's inaugural issuances of 20-year and 30-year RMB green bonds, representing the longest-dated RMB bonds issued by the Government to date. They established new benchmarks for the market and further reinforced the demonstration effect of the Sustainable Bond Programme. The bonds also enriched the range of offshore RMB investment products available in Hong Kong. Moreover, the enthusiastic response from global investors to the Government's green bond issuances reflects their recognition of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development.  To encourage more regional borrowers to use Hong Kong's financing platform to raise sustainable development funding, the HKMA has continued to implement the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme launched in May 2021, which provides subsidies for eligible green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong. The scheme has been well-received by the industry. As of end-2024, it had approved grants for approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, with a total value of over USD 140 billion. The scheme was extended by three years to 2027 in May 2024, with its coverage expanded to transition bonds and loans. The extension and expansion of the scheme aim to encourage borrowers in relevant sectors in the region to utilise Hong Kong's transition financing platform to progressively reduce carbon emissions.  - Approved grants for approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong with a total value of over USD 140 billion (as of end-2024) - Extended by three years to 2027, with coverage expanded to transition financing instruments  Meanwhile, the HKMA has been actively promoting Hong Kong's sustainable financing platform, yielding positive results. In August, the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government issued offshore local government bonds in Hong Kong for the fourth time, totalling RMB 7 billion, comprising RMB 2.7 billion in green bonds, RMB 1 billion in sustainable bonds and RMB 900 million in social bonds. In September, the Guangdong Provincial People's Government issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the first time, totalling RMB 5 billion, including RMB 1.5 billion in green bonds. In October, the Hainan Provincial People's Government also issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the third time, totalling RMB 3 billion, including RMB 1 billion in blue bonds and RMB 1 billion in sustainable bonds. These bond issuance activities have repeatedly highlighted Hong Kong's unique role in facilitating the flow of green and sustainable capital between the Mainland and the rest of the world.  Through these various measures, Hong Kong has been able to consolidate its position as the preferred platform for sustainable financing in Asia. According to statistics published by the International Capital Market Association, Hong Kong remained the largest hub for arranging the issuance of international green and sustainable bonds in Asia in 2024, with a total of USD 43.1 billion in such bonds arranged through Hong Kong, accounting for 45% of the regional total.  To catalyse sustainable finance innovation, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing two landmark batches of tokenised green bonds in 2023 and 2024, namely the world's first tokenised government green bonds and the world's first multi-currency digital bonds. These issuances demonstrate the Government's support for market participants in the region in applying asset tokenisation and innovative technologies in the green and sustainable finance space. The HKMA also launched the Digital Bond Grant Scheme in November to promote the issuance of digital bonds in Hong Kong, including digital green bonds, thereby encouraging and supporting innovation in Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance market.  The working group on sustainable disclosure under the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group) has been working on the adoption of International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) Standards in Hong Kong. In December 2024, the Government published the Hong Kong Sustainability Disclosure Roadmap, providing a clear pathway for large public interest entities to fully adopt the ISSB Standards no later than 2028. The HKMA has been working closely with local and international partners to support entities at different stages of readiness in achieving high-quality sustainable disclosure, making sustainable disclosure more accessible and inclusive.  Worthy of note, we have continued to encourage the adoption of the Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Unlisted Companies (Questionnaire), which was launched by the Steering Group in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Questionnaire provides an easy-to-use disclosure template to facilitate sustainable disclosure by companies, including small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). An electronic version of the Questionnaire was launched in February 2024 to facilitate online completion by companies (see the QR code below). The HKMA is refining the Questionnaire based on industry feedback and the latest international developments to make it more user-friendly, including identifying the core questions in the Questionnaire and providing common use-case scenarios. We are also seeking to improve the compatibility of the Questionnaire with other supporting tools on the Steering Group's website. For more information on the Questionnaire, please refer to the relevant webpage.  The HKMA leads by example by making high-quality sustainable disclosures in its Sustainability Report in accordance with the latest global standards, demonstrating its commitment. The report covers comprehensive content on the HKMA's climate-related institutional operational risks, as well as plans and progress towards achieving climate targets. For details of our own operational sustainable disclosures, please refer to the chapter on "A Sustainable HKMA."  Given the rapidly evolving sustainable finance market, to bridge the knowledge and talent gap, the HKMA is stepping up skills training efforts in the banking sector and fostering knowledge sharing with other regulators and international stakeholders. To enhance the knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners in sustainable finance, the HKMA and the Hong Kong Institute of Bankers (HKIB) launched the Foundation Level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the Enhanced Competency Framework (ECF) for Banking Practitioners in July 2023. The module aims to help banking professionals acquire knowledge in green and sustainable finance in a more effective manner and develop related professional competencies, covering four key areas of work: (1) Green and Sustainable Finance Products and Services; (2) Sustainable/Climate Risk Management; (3) Sustainable Disclosure and Reporting; and (4) Sustainable Strategy, Compliance and Controls. In addition, the Professional Level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module, targeting mid-to-senior banking practitioners responsible for relevant work, was launched in November.  To provide the necessary training for banking practitioners, the HKIB, as the managing body of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module, launched the Foundation Level training programme for the module in May. Following the launch of the Professional Level in November, the HKMA will work with the banking industry in 2025 to develop the training programme for the Professional Level. To better understand the further skills and training needs of the banking sector, the HKMA is currently working with the banking industry to conduct the research on "Future Bankers 2026–2030," with the aim of publishing the findings in 2025. This joint research is a follow-up to the "Future Bankers 2021–2025" document published in June 2020. The findings of the follow-up research will serve as an important reference for the industry in formulating and adjusting its talent training strategies and initiatives to support the sustainable development of the banking sector.  The HKMA has also continued to assist in implementing the Government-funded Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Programme through collaboration with the Steering Group, which subsidises practitioners, graduates and students in undertaking sustainable finance-related training. As of December 2024, the programme had 85 international and local courses registered as eligible training courses, and over 5,700 reimbursement applications had been approved. The Government announced in the 2025–26 Budget that the programme would be extended to 2028.  The HKMA is committed to leveraging its experience to promote skills training and knowledge sharing through regional and international collaboration. As a founding member of the Capacity Building Alliance for Sustainable Investment (CASI), the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office co-organised a two-day training workshop with CASI in Hong Kong in June, with discussions focused on global sustainable finance markets, policy frameworks and innovative instruments. In addition, the HKMA supported the establishment of a Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ) regional chapter in Hong Kong in October, and will leverage GFANZ's network and expertise to strengthen skills training in transition planning and transition finance.

As a significant global asset owner and manager, the HKMA actively leads the development of green and sustainable finance. Drawing on its experience in demonstrating that financial performance and positive impact can be mutually reinforcing, the HKMA adheres to a responsible investment philosophy in managing the Exchange Fund, prioritising sustainable assets and requiring its external investment managers to actively exercise asset ownership. Guided by the principle of "preserving capital first, achieving long-term growth", the HKMA invests prudently in the belief that due regard for environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors helps mitigate investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As a committed signatory to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the HKMA is dedicated to advancing its responsible investment work. We place particular importance on sustainability, especially the pressing issue of climate change, with the aim of enhancing the resilience of the Exchange Fund and achieving better risk-adjusted long-term returns. We integrate ESG factors in a pragmatic and orderly manner, continuously exploring various investment instruments to channel capital into sustainable investments across different asset classes (Exhibit 1). Leveraging its role as a major investor, the HKMA contributes to the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. In September, the HKMA published the "HKMA ESG Expectations" and made the document available to investment partners through annual ESG workshops and the HKMA website. We work with like-minded investors, regulators and international organisations to develop industry standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment across the financial industry and among central banks. Through these collaborative efforts, we strive to advance a future where finance and sustainable development go hand in hand. In October, the HKMA published the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" (the "Action Plan"), articulating its commitment to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund "investment portfolio" by 2050 or earlier, as well as mobilising partners to support the transition to a low-carbon economy, further reinforcing its commitment to investing in a sustainable future. The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee (EFAC), chaired by the Financial Secretary, sets the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office (EFIO) in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The overarching guiding principle establishes the tone for the HKMA to pursue responsible investment while balancing the Exchange Fund's investment objectives. The Investment Committee under EFAC, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for overseeing ESG and climate-related risks pertaining to Exchange Fund investments. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management guidelines, and monitors implementation through regular reports from the Sustainable Investment Team of the EFIO. As illustrated in Exhibit 2, the ESG Committee under the EFIO, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, is responsible for coordinating and overseeing the EFIO's various ESG initiatives. Motions and progress discussed at the ESG Committee's quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the EFIO. In addition, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and attended by the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Strategy Officer of the EFIO, meets regularly to provide guidance on ESG policies and measures across different functions of the HKMA, including the EFIO, in pursuit of the HKMA's overarching ESG objectives. The Sustainable Investment Team works closely with different EFIO teams on the integration of ESG factors, and assists senior EFIO staff in managing ESG — particularly climate-related — risks and opportunities across various investments:  - Public Market Investments — The Credit, Compliance and Oversight Committee, comprising senior EFIO staff, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models with input from the Sustainable Investment Team, and monitors the ESG profile of the fixed income portfolio through periodic reports from the Risk Management and Oversight Department. In addition, the Sustainable Investment Team participates from an ESG perspective in the selection, appointment and monitoring of external investment managers for the equity portfolio (see the "Promoting Active Ownership" section under "Risk Management" on page 39 for details).  - Private Market Investments — The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the ESG-related assessments made by the private markets investment and risk management teams for each investment proposal.  The HKMA recognises that the physical and transition risks, as well as opportunities, arising from climate change will affect the long-term financial performance of Exchange Fund investments. The Emissions Gap Report 2024 published by the United Nations Environment Programme projects that global average temperatures will rise by 2.6 to 3.1 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels unless there is rapid, large-scale global mobilisation to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. The uncertainty surrounding policy changes, technological developments and behavioural shifts in response to rising temperatures may exacerbate transition risks, leading to increased market volatility and affecting asset valuations. At the same time, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events also poses additional risks of physical damage and financial losses to investments. Amidst these challenges, the shift by governments and industries towards sustainable solutions also creates investment opportunities in low-carbon solutions, emerging technologies and sustainable infrastructure that may offer attractive long-term prospects. The HKMA believes that investing in a sustainable future is aligned with the Exchange Fund's investment objectives, and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors when integrating ESG considerations. The HKMA has set a target for the Exchange Fund "investment portfolio" to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, and continues to make progress towards this goal through an orderly three-pronged approach (see Exhibit 3). The HKMA published the "Action Plan" in 2024, which reinforces the Exchange Fund's commitments and efforts relating to climate transition (see Exhibit 4). To support the transition to a low-carbon economy, the HKMA favours active engagement over exclusion or divestment from investable assets.  Investing in a Sustainable Future Exchange Fund "investment portfolio" to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier - Actively expand the scope and diversity of sustainable investments, particularly climate transition-themed investments in both public and private markets - Integrate ESG factors in each investment decision, with particular focus on climate change and transition prospect considerations - Establish clear ESG expectations that are consistent with international standards and best practices, and require all external investment managers, investee companies and counterparties to comply with them - Committed to reducing the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund's equity portfolio by 67% from the 2017 level by 2030 or earlier  Supporting Transition in the Region Through Investment - Continue engaging with external investment managers to optimise investment opportunities that drive transition - Continue to identify and prioritise quality investment opportunities that promote Asia's transition and generate positive global impact  First, maintaining a diversified and resilient portfolio is crucial to achieving the Exchange Fund's primary investment objectives. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, potentially affecting investment returns and risks. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA is able to seize opportunities to invest in companies that are undergoing transition and possess superior technologies and sound corporate governance to navigate evolving global climate trends, including those in high-emission industries.  Second, addressing climate change requires the transition of core "brown" industries. Merely excluding investments or divesting does not address the issue of carbon emissions. Instead, the HKMA supports these industries through the deployment of strategic capital and active exercise of asset ownership, encouraging them to transition to sustainable and low-carbon operating practices, thereby driving beneficial change for them and for the world. Net-zero investment approaches have evolved from a preference for green or low-carbon assets to encompassing assets with credible transition prospects, in order to drive economy-wide decarbonisation.  As a global asset owner, the HKMA recognises that the long-term resilience of its portfolio depends not only on adjustments within the portfolio itself, but also on broader economic transition. While there is no perfect single solution, the HKMA refined its responsible investment strategy in 2024, adopting a comprehensive and diversified approach to drive transition while supporting the Exchange Fund and global net-zero objectives. The strategy combines top-down and bottom-up tools, including the integration of ESG factors and stewardship into fundamental analysis, portfolio decarbonisation tilts, and thematic investments targeting asset classes aligned with net-zero pathways. In public markets, this may involve tilting the portfolio towards ESG leaders or providers of climate solutions, complemented by active exercise of asset ownership to drive corporate transition. In private markets, the focus may be more on investments that facilitate transition. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continuously identifies investment opportunities that can promote climate transition while enhancing the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund's portfolio.  Sustainable investments across different asset classes account for over 10% of the Exchange Fund "investment portfolio", with financial performance comparable to the relevant portfolio benchmarks (Exhibit 5).  - Public Market Investments — The HKMA launched an active global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition, and extended the application of customised low-carbon equity indices to two additional portfolios managed by external investment managers. The HKMA also continues to seek green, social and sustainability (GSS) bonds that offer competitive returns while funding sustainable projects (see the "Enhancing Sustainability Through GSS Bonds" section for a relevant case study).  - Private Market Investments — The HKMA is committed to building a resilient long-term growth portfolio by capturing investment opportunities aligned with climate and energy transition themes. Leveraging its extensive network and expertise, the HKMA actively identifies and evaluates investment opportunities that can accelerate the energy transition, including through establishing strategic partnerships with multilateral organisations (see the "Collaborating to Address Climate Challenges in Asia and Beyond" section for examples).  - Passive portfolios benchmarked against ESG indices - Customised decarbonisation strategies for passive and active quantitative portfolios benchmarked against non-ESG indices - Active portfolios with a governance theme - Active ESG portfolios themed around sustainability and climate transition - Projects with sustainable characteristics, such as renewable energy infrastructure, and buildings and warehouses with green certification - Funds themed around energy transition and decarbonisation in global, Asian and Global South contexts - Green, social and sustainability bonds - A green bond fund managed by an international organisation - The Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Programme (MCPP) managed by the International Finance Corporation, focusing on sustainable projects in emerging markets - The "MCPP One Planet" programme, providing climate-related investments in emerging markets aligned with the Paris Agreement  The HKMA invested in green bonds issued by a quasi-government institution. The proceeds from the green bonds were allocated to multiple projects, including upgrading ageing equipment at several wastewater treatment facilities. These upgrades encompass optimising monitoring and control systems and pump performance to generate positive environmental benefits through wastewater management, waste reduction and recycling processes. In addition to the continuous treatment of wastewater and sludge, the facilities compost or repurpose dewatered sludge to produce fertiliser, charcoal, cement and other construction materials, achieving a sludge recovery rate of up to 100%. The facilities also utilise gas generated during the sludge treatment process to provide energy for boilers and generate electricity.  The HKMA invested in green bonds issued by a multilateral development bank. The bonds provided funding for multiple projects, including the rehabilitation of a national canal system. As one of the country's largest irrigation systems, the canal is designed to divert excess water from rivers to arid regions. The primary objective of the project is to restore the deteriorating canal lining to prevent seepage, conserve water, improve water use efficiency and reclaim flood-affected areas. In addition, the project conducts skills training for local stakeholders to promote the adoption and effective use of modern irrigation technologies such as micro-irrigation and sustainable farming practices.

The HKMA is committed to being a responsible and sustainable institution. One of the key priorities in 2024 in delivering on this commitment was a plan to bring forward the target for achieving net-zero emissions from its institutional operations to 2030, 20 years ahead of the original target, in alignment with the Sustainable Finance Action Agenda. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA is also committed to fostering employee training and wellbeing, and to advancing financial inclusion and enhancing the public's financial literacy. The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is the principal decision-making body for institutional sustainability initiatives. To demonstrate the HKMA's commitment to climate change, the Steering Committee approved in October 2024 a new target for the HKMA to achieve net-zero emissions from its institutional operations by 2030, as part of the Sustainable Finance Action Agenda (Action Agenda). At the departmental level, the Assistant Chief Executive (Institutional Development and Operations) provides guidance on implementing sustainability measures relating to institutional operations, employee wellbeing and community engagement, and reports to the Steering Committee on a regular basis. The Administration Division serves as the coordinator and central hub for implementing, communicating and reporting on institutional sustainability measures. The Green Office Task Force and the Volunteer Services Team, comprising staff from different operational departments, provide an additional layer of support: the former is a platform for generating ideas and making recommendations on how to create a greener working environment, while the latter aims to cultivate a culture of volunteerism among staff. In recognition of the HKMA's dedication to caring for the environment, its employees and the community at large, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has presented the HKMA with the "Caring Organisation with 15 Years+" logo for 18 consecutive years from 2006 to 2024. The HKMA's sustainability strategy continues to be structured around three pillars: Environment, Employees and Social Responsibility. - Focus on decarbonisation and digitalisation of the HKMA's day-to-day operations, with the target of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030 - Adopt green procurement requirements in accordance with government guidelines - Promote greener practices in the financial industry and the community at large - Build an engaged workforce and talent pool to achieve the HKMA's strategic objectives - Create a work environment that promotes collaboration and is caring and inclusive, valuing diversity and strengthening employees' sense of belonging - Provide a quality work environment that encourages a healthy lifestyle - Foster a community-caring culture - Incorporate social considerations into procurement processes and supply chain management - Promote financial inclusion and enhance public financial literacy through consumer education activities The HKMA takes climate change seriously and leads by example. In October 2024, the HKMA announced its plan to bring forward the target for achieving net-zero emissions from its institutional operations to 2030, 20 years ahead of its earlier commitment, as part of the Action Agenda. The HKMA has revised its roadmap for the net-zero transition, with a focus on responsibly managing the environmental impact of its day-to-day operations, concentrating on reducing carbon emissions, saving energy, reducing paper consumption and recycling waste, while fully leveraging improvements in the fuel mix for electricity generation by local power companies. In addition, the HKMA has built a digitalised working environment to improve efficiency while at the same time reducing its carbon footprint. Furthermore, recognising the importance of fostering a culture of sustainability, the HKMA encourages staff to actively adopt sustainable practices through ongoing promotional programmes and activities. In pursuit of the primary net-zero target by 2030, the HKMA has been exploring the use of carbon inset tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions and procuring low-carbon options wherever possible. In this connection, since 2023, the HKMA has been fully offsetting the carbon emissions from air travel by purchasing sustainable aviation fuel and participating in a carbon offset programme. The HKMA will extend its carbon insetting and carbon offset programmes to cover all other major carbon emissions. In addition to the above environmental commitments relating to physical operations, the HKMA continues to drive the market's low-carbon transition, ranging from introducing electronic document submission and processing procedures to promoting electronic payments and collecting coins for return to circulation. The remainder of this chapter details the HKMA's strategies in leading green practices, as well as promoting employee wellbeing and community care. Under the HKMA's overall institutional risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for monitoring and reviewing potential risks and threats to the HKMA's day-to-day operations, including those arising from climate change. To more effectively assess the potential operational impact of climate change, the HKMA has identified various climate-related risks and reviewed their actual and potential impacts. To address climate-related risks while ensuring business continuity, the design of the HKMA's offices incorporates a number of measures to mitigate potential physical hazards, fire and other emergencies. In addition, the HKMA regularly updates its contingency plans to incorporate comprehensive measures covering not only the offices, but also communications and computer facilities. The HKMA conducts regular evacuation and back-up facility activation drills to ensure that staff are always prepared to implement contingency measures. The HKMA has also been monitoring the transition risks it faces by tracking its greenhouse gas emissions from operations, waste generation, and energy and paper consumption. The HKMA's latest climate target is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions for Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 from its institutional operations by 2030. These targets have been formulated with reference to the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) methodology. The HKMA uses the Greenhouse Gas Protocol to measure and report its institutional emissions. Scope 1 emissions are direct emissions from petrol vehicles. Given the nature of its operations, the HKMA's principal greenhouse gas emissions are Scope 2 indirect greenhouse gas emissions from electricity generated by burning fossil fuels. In the absence of data from individual suppliers, the HKMA adopts a conservative approach to estimate the major Scope 3 emissions from purchased goods (including capital goods) and services. Other relevant Scope 3 emissions include waste sent to landfills, and staff air travel and commuting. Details of the calculations for 2023 and 2024 are set out in the Performance Summary on page 50. The HKMA's disclosed performance data have been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The scope and basis of verification are set out in the Verification Statement appended at the end of this report. The HKMA leads by example, adhering to the same climate-related standards it expects the banks it regulates and the financial system it oversees to follow. As a first step towards green mobility, the HKMA began replacing its petrol vehicles with electric vehicles in 2024, and will continue this effort in 2025 to achieve full green mobility. The HKMA continues to incorporate green considerations into the design, operation and maintenance of its offices. Specifically, during the renovation works in 2024, the HKMA reused existing furniture and fitting materials or traded in old items for new ones to minimise waste. To improve overall energy efficiency, the HKMA regularly reviews energy consumption and energy-saving measures in offices and data centres, and adopted a modular uninterruptible power supply system design in the 2024 data centre facility upgrade project to further optimise the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of its BEAM Plus-certified data centre. This design enables flexible capacity expansion, improved partial-load operational efficiency, and features advanced cooling technology and higher power density, contributing to reduced overall energy consumption. The HKMA has strengthened internal virtual collaboration through the digital workplace, complemented by streamlined workflows, to effectively reduce paper consumption. In addition, the HKMA has extended the service life of mobile and desktop devices in alignment with manufacturers' software update cycles, which prolongs the devices' secure operational life. To reduce office waste, the HKMA follows the "4R" principle of refuse, reduce, reuse and recycle, and conducts regular waste audits to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. The HKMA has placed recycling bins for different materials at various convenient locations around the office. To improve the recycling rate, the HKMA added collection bins for beverage cartons and plastic fruit net bags in 2024. In addition, since November 2022, the HKMA has been sending collected food waste to a waste-to-energy centre in Hong Kong. In May 2024, the HKMA participated in the Environmental Protection Department's "Event Waste Reduction Pledge", committing to taking measures to reduce waste generated at various events. The HKMA continues to prioritise the procurement of goods that meet the environmental specifications on the government's "Green Procurement List", particularly electrical appliances and office consumables. To reduce the carbon footprint from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to plan their trips carefully, such as combining multiple journeys where possible when attending overseas events. At the institutional level, the HKMA has been purchasing sustainable aviation fuel since 2023 to reduce annual air travel carbon emissions by approximately 10%. In addition, the HKMA participates in a Gold Standard-certified carbon offset programme to offset the remaining air travel carbon emissions; this programme focuses on renewable energy production and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, the HKMA arranged a number of learning activities for staff, such as seminars and guided tours of waste-to-energy facilities, to enhance staff awareness of environmental sustainability issues. The HKMA held its first "HKMA Green Month" from Earth Day on 22 April 2024 through the entire month of May, with the theme "Think Green, Live Green, Work Green". This was a valuable opportunity to demonstrate the HKMA's commitment and momentum in promoting environmental sustainability in internal operations. Activities throughout the event included a "Sustainability BINGO Scorecard" to encourage staff to adopt green living practices, a "Save the Planet" quiz game, and a kokedama indoor plant cultivation workshop originating from Japan, as well as the sharing of waste audit results and an introduction to best recycling practices by a community recycling centre operator.
