To maintain the momentum of "Green Month", the HKMA launched an approximately six-month recycling campaign in October, highlighting responsible waste management and reminding staff that small changes in individual habits can contribute significantly to improving the institution's overall recycling performance. One highlight of the campaign was the launch of a short video entitled "Green Action Tips", featuring several senior management members sharing recycling tips. The campaign also featured a series of screensavers, eye-catching posters, intranet articles and electronic reminders to encourage staff to practise waste reduction and increase recycling. Towards the end of 2024, the HKMA conducted a staff survey to gauge their awareness of sustainability and gather their views on proposed green office measures. The survey results will help inform the formulation of future sustainability training activities and waste management strategies. As Hong Kong's de facto central banking institution, the HKMA sees itself as an important agent of change, and is therefore committed to leading the acceleration of the low-carbon transition and promoting sustainable practices in the financial industry and society as a whole. The HKMA has introduced a number of measures to enhance the efficiency of external processes. Following the successful launch of the Common Submission Platform in 2023, the HKMA expanded the platform's scope in 2024 to cover non-bank institutions, such as stored value facility operators, to facilitate their submission of certain regulatory data. The expansion of the platform aims to further streamline the submission process for reporting entities, providing a more seamless experience for all users while reinforcing the HKMA's commitment to sustainability. Other new measures introduced in 2024 include the SurveyTool, which allows banks to respond to HKMA questionnaires through a streamlined submission process, and an intelligent information and document management system that provides users with a central platform featuring advanced search capabilities for bank-related documents.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) conducted an independent verification of the environmental data (the "Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). The Data covers total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), and GHG emissions from business air travel for 2024, together with their respective intensity figures. In addition, the Data includes Scope 3 GHG emissions for 2023 and 2024 arising from purchased goods and services, capital goods, fuel- and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), and employee commuting, along with their corresponding intensities. The HKMA's GHG emissions data were compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (GHG Protocol) jointly published by the World Resources Institute (WRI) and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD). The verification scope covers a total of 6 office and warehouse assets, comprising 5 offices located at: 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and 5) International Commerce Centre, as well as a warehouse at 6) Lok Sing Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance on the accuracy and reliability of the Data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanism. Within the scope of verification, HKQAA reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from the 6 assets. The verification was conducted in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), "Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information", issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board (IAASB). The verification procedures were specifically designed to form an opinion and conclusion to achieve a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was carried out in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing selected sample data back to their sources, and examined the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checking, as well as conducting reliability tests. The verification process also included verifying internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with representatives responsible for preparing the Data, and selecting representative data and information for review. The relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also subject to detailed examination during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of the Data. Our verification work is entirely independent and impartial. The HKQAA verification team was not involved in the data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, HKQAA provides reasonable assurance and concludes that: - The Data are materially accurate and reliable; and - The HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is adequate.  Shen Xiaoyin Verification Manager Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency March 2025
